name: Links

# Ported from the template's links.yml (issue #115, R3/R5; hive-mind principle
# #12, "documentation validation"). Nothing in this repository had ever checked
# a URL. Reproduced against the tree as it was at 024dd6a, the run reports 113
# failures over 16 files (107 distinct URLs, log in
# dev/log/issues/115/pulls/116/logs/lychee-baseline-024dd6a.log): 85 GHCR
# package pages the README advertised for images that have never been pushed,
# 14 relative links to files that are not there - CI logs GitHub's 90-day
# retention had already removed, and paths off by one `../` - three dead
# upstream URLs, and a handful of hosts that answer a link checker with 429,
# 503 or a TLS handshake failure.
#
# Reproduce locally with the same image and the same arguments:
#
#   docker run --rm -v "$PWD:[REDACTED]" -w /repo lycheeverse/lychee:0.24.2 \
#     --no-progress --include-fragments --max-retries 2 --timeout 30 \
#     --exclude-path dev/log './**/*.md'
#
# dev/log/ is excluded because it holds verbatim copies of other projects'
# documentation, collected as issue evidence; their links are not ours to fix.
# Known false positives - login-gated pages, rate-limiting hosts - are in
# .lycheeignore, each with the reason it is there.

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '**.md'
      - '.lycheeignore'
      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
      - 'scripts/ci/check-web-archive.mjs'
      - 'scripts/ci/recheck-broken-links.mjs'
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      - '**.md'
      - '.lycheeignore'
      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
      - 'scripts/ci/check-web-archive.mjs'
      - 'scripts/ci/recheck-broken-links.mjs'
  # Weekly: a link rots without anyone touching this repository. The three dead
  # upstream URLs this port found had all been correct when they were written.
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 2'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # actions/checkout's first act is `git init`, and a git with no configured
  # `init.defaultBranch` answers it with a thirteen-line advice block - "Using
  # 'master' as the name for the initial branch... this default branch name will
  # change" - at the top of every job log. 19 checkouts in the runs issue #121
  # lists printed 247 lines of it, in jobs where nothing was wrong. No step can
  # fix it, because it is printed before the first step of ours runs; git reads
  # configuration from the environment too, and the environment is there from
  # the start. Ported from the js template, which carries the same three lines
  # with the same reasoning.
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  link-checker:
    name: links / lychee
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # A full run is ~10s cached, ~30s cold. 10 minutes is the ceiling that stops
    # one slow external host from holding a runner.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-link-checker
      cancel-in-progress: true
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # A pull_request checkout is GitHub's merge preview, computed when the
      # pull request was last synchronised and never recomputed as main moves.
      # Merge the base branch first, so this job reports on what merging would
      # actually produce (issue #115, best practice #7).
      - name: Simulate a fresh merge with the base branch
        uses: ./.github/actions/simulate-fresh-merge

      # A `uses:` step takes the budget GitHub applies to a whole step, since it
      # cannot be routed through scripts/ci/run-with-budget-warning.sh (issue
      # #121, docs/CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md). The slowest run measured took 30
      # seconds; 5 minutes bounds a slow external host without waiting for the
      # job cap, which would report the job *cancelled* and skip the reporting
      # steps below - including the recovery pass that tells a false positive
      # from a real broken link.
      #
      # --include-fragments: without it lychee resolves a link's *document* and
      # stops, so `docs/RELEASING.md#making-the-ghcr-packages-public` passes as
      # long as the file exists, whatever the headings inside it say - and an
      # anchor is exactly the part of a link that a heading rename breaks. This
      # gate had never checked one (issue #121). Measured on this tree: a
      # fixture that renames the target heading of a same-file and a cross-file
      # anchor passes without the flag and fails with it; over the whole corpus
      # the flag reports 681 links, 473 unique, 667 OK, 0 errors in 14.6s, after
      # the three genuinely dead remote anchors it found were fixed (docker's
      # #entrypoint-default-command-to-execute-at-runtime, jpetazzo/dind's
      # #warning-..., and a GitHub docs page that moved). Evidence:
      # dev/log/issues/121/pulls/122/doc-fragments/. It applies to remote
      # anchors too, which is why the number of requests does not change: lychee
      # already fetched those pages, it just discarded their ids.
      - name: Check links with lychee
        id: lychee
        timeout-minutes: 5
        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
        with:
          args: >-
            --no-progress
            --cache
            --max-cache-age 1d
            --include-fragments
            --max-retries 2
            --timeout 30
            --exclude-path dev/log
            './**/*.md'
          # Not a failure yet: a broken link that the Wayback Machine has
          # archived gets a concrete replacement suggested below, which is more
          # use to the author than a bare red X.
          fail: false
          output: lychee/out.md
          jobSummary: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Set up Node
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # lychee classifies an error by the phase it happened in, and a failure
      # during connect is never retried - `--max-retries` does not apply to it
      # (lycheeverse/lychee#2297). So a healthy host that answers one TCP reset,
      # which a CI address range collects from rate-limiting and load-shedding
      # hosts, is reported broken without a single retry and fails this gate:
      # a false positive (issue #121). Ask those URLs again, outside lychee. A
      # temporary HTTP error (408, 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504) can also recover:
      # PR #132 failed on two healthy GitHub docs links answering 503. Retry
      # those within the same wall-clock budget; only an accepted status can
      # recover them. Permanent failures such as 404 remain final. URLs with
      # fragments stay final because the recovery's HEAD cannot check anchors.
      - name: Re-check unanswered links and temporary HTTP errors
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0
        id: recheck
        run: node scripts/ci/recheck-broken-links.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
          RECOVERED_OUTPUT: lychee/recovered.txt

      # `!= 'true'`, never `== 'false'`: a skipped or crashed re-check leaves
      # the output empty, and only the `!=` form reads that as "still failing".
      - name: Look for Web Archive replacements
        if: >-
          steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0 &&
          steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true'
        run: node scripts/ci/check-web-archive.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
          RECOVERED_URLS: lychee/recovered.txt

      - name: Fail if broken links were found
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0 &&
          steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error title=links::lychee found broken links."
          echo
          echo "An archive URL is a suggested replacement; it does not make the"
          echo "live link valid. For each broken link, in order of preference:"
          echo "  1. Point at the current location of the same content."
          echo "  2. Point at the archive.org snapshot suggested above."
          echo "  3. Pin a GitHub link to the commit that still holds the file."
          echo "  4. Delete the link if the content is gone and not worth citing."
          echo "  5. Add the URL to .lycheeignore *with a reason* - but only if"
          echo "     the link is correct and merely unverifiable (login-gated,"
          echo "     rate-limited, bot-blocked). A dead link is not a false"
          echo "     positive, and silencing it is the defect issue #115 is about."
          echo
          echo "Reproduce locally:"
          echo "  docker run --rm -v \"\$PWD:[REDACTED]\" -w /repo lycheeverse/lychee:0.24.2 \\"
          echo "    --no-progress --include-fragments --max-retries 2 --timeout 30 \\"
          echo "    --exclude-path dev/log './**/*.md'"
          exit 1

      - name: The gate's own fixtures still hold
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: bash experiments/test-issue115-links-gate.sh

  # === TERMINAL STATUS GATE ===
  #
  # The job that makes every other job's result reach the run's conclusion
  # (issue #121, reference-template best practice "every workflow gets a
  # terminal status gate").
  #
  # GitHub derives a run's conclusion from its jobs, and one cancellation
  # outranks any number of failures - so a run holding a failed job can still
  # come out grey, and everything that reads the run rather than each job (the
  # badge, `gh run list`, the run list quoted in issue #121 itself) reads that
  # as "no verdict" rather than "something broke". A gate's own conclusion is a
  # job conclusion, so when it errors the run is red no matter what else was
  # cancelled. The rationale, the measured run and the supersede-versus-overrun
  # rule are in scripts/ci/check-pipeline-status.sh.
  #
  # `!cancelled()`, not `always()`: cancelling a whole run is somebody's
  # decision and repainting it red would be a false positive, so this job is
  # skipped there. `cancelled()` is run-level, so a job cancelled on its own -
  # an overrun, or a per-job concurrency group firing - still reaches the gate.
  #
  # `needs` must name every other job in this file, or a job's result cannot
  # reach here at all. That is not left to review:
  # scripts/ci/check-status-gate-covers-all-jobs.mjs derives the list from this
  # workflow and fails when the two disagree.
  pipeline-status:
    name: pipeline-status
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [link-checker]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Anonymous `git ls-remote` is enough to resolve the branch head, which is
      # how the script tells a superseded run from an overrun; no token is
      # persisted for it.
      - name: Check pipeline status
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-pipeline-status.sh
name: Measure Disk Space and Update README

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - 'scripts/ubuntu-24-server-install.sh'
      - 'scripts/measure-disk-space.sh'
      - 'scripts/update-readme-sizes.sh'
      - 'Dockerfile'
      - '.github/workflows/measure-disk-space.yml'
  # The measurement itself takes ~3 hours and pushes to main, so it cannot run
  # on a pull request. What CAN run on a pull request is everything that decides
  # whether the measurement is going to work at all — and it has to, because
  # this workflow only ever ran after the merge. Run 33972074753 (main, commit
  # 42be663) is the case in point: `NODE_MAJOR: unbound variable` was
  # introduced, reviewed and merged without a single job ever executing the
  # changed script (issue #115).
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      - 'scripts/ubuntu-24-server-install.sh'
      - 'scripts/measure-disk-space.sh'
      - 'scripts/update-readme-sizes.sh'
      - 'ubuntu/24.04/common.sh'
      - 'data/disk-space-measurements.json'
      - '.github/workflows/measure-disk-space.yml'
      # The preflight and validation jobs, which are what a pull request can
      # run here, are the only place these three are executed at all. They are
      # deliberately absent from the push filter above: editing a validator
      # should re-run the validation, not spend three hours measuring d…1930 tokens truncated…   starts (v1.7.8, v1.7.10).
      # Measured against fixtures for all three plus a YAML merge key, v1.7.7
      # reports one finding and describes it wrongly; v1.7.12 reports four:
      # experiments/reproduce-issue121-actionlint-version-gap.sh. Against this
      # repository as it stands both are clean, so the bump costs nothing now
      # and is the only thing here that can make those three findings - the
      # coverage gate below cannot see a dead `paths:` entry that has a live
      # sibling.
      - uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint@sha256:b1934ee5f1c509618f2508e6eb47ee0d3520686341fec936f3b79331f9315667 # v1.7.12
        with:
          args: -color

      # actionlint is the only thing above that reads these files as YAML, and it
      # needs docker - so the pre-commit hook cannot run it, and an unparseable
      # workflow was committable (issue #123). The three gates below read
      # workflows line by line, which is right for the questions they ask and
      # means none of them can tell a file they disagree with from a file no
      # parser accepts: release-full.yml was not YAML and all three passed it.
      # This establishes that floor offline, in milliseconds, for both.
      - name: Every workflow and composite action parses as YAML
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-workflow-yaml.sh

      - name: The YAML gate's own fixtures still hold
        run: bash experiments/test-issue123-workflow-yaml.sh

      # actionlint validates a workflow's syntax; it cannot know that a job was
      # left out of the terminal gate's `needs` and so cannot turn the run red
      # (issue #121). That requirement is derived from each workflow rather than
      # kept in a list, so adding a job to any file here fails this step until
      # the gate names it.
      - name: Every workflow's status gate covers every job in it
        run: node scripts/ci/check-status-gate-covers-all-jobs.mjs .github/workflows/*.yml

      # The same argument one level down (issue #121). A long step's execution
      # budget only reports the overrun if it expires *before* the job's
      # `timeout-minutes` backstop cancels the job; a budget that meets or
      # exceeds its cap is a check that can never fire, and the run goes grey
      # with no indication of which step ran long. This derives both numbers
      # from the workflow and fails when a budget claims too much of its cap -
      # per matrix leg, because this repository sizes caps and budgets per leg.
      - name: Every execution budget fits inside its job's timeout
        run: node scripts/ci/check-timeout-budgets.mjs .github/workflows/*.yml

      # And one level up again (issue #121). A `paths:` filter is the cheapest
      # way to build a check that cannot fail: the job exists, the gate works,
      # its fixtures pass, and because the filter matches none of the files the
      # gate reads, the pull request that breaks exactly what it was written for
      # never starts it - nothing red, nothing skipped, just absent from the
      # list. scripts.yml ran the JavaScript syntax gate under a filter of
      # '**.sh', 'ubuntu/**' and 'tests/**' for a day. This asks, of every
      # script a workflow runs, whether every file it reads can start a run.
      - name: Every gate can be started by the files it reads
        run: node scripts/ci/check-workflow-path-coverage.mjs

      # The gate's own fixtures: throwaway repositories whose filters are known
      # to cover or to miss, so a change to the pattern translation - GitHub's
      # `*` stops at a slash and `**` does not - fails here rather than by
      # quietly passing a repository it should have reported.
      - name: Path-coverage fixtures
        run: bash experiments/test-issue121-path-coverage.sh

      # Every job log used to open with git's thirteen-line "Using 'master' as
      # the name for the initial branch" advice, because actions/checkout runs
      # `git init` before any step can configure it. The fix is three `env:`
      # entries per workflow, and the thing that rots is the next workflow
      # added without them - so this reads all of them, every time one changes.
      - name: Git advice hints
        run: bash experiments/test-issue121-git-init-hint.sh

      # actions/checkout authenticates by writing the job's token into
      # .git/config, and unless told otherwise leaves it there for every later
      # step. Thirty of this repository's fifty-five checkouts said nothing, so
      # thirty jobs kept it - `js / build-js-amd64` for 427 seconds while a
      # docker build ran with the workspace as its context, against 1.1-2.1s in
      # the jobs that had been hardened. zizmor audits this (`artipacked`) and
      # ran on every one of them, but reports at severity Low and the job below
      # floors at medium: filtered out thirty times (issue #121). This asks the
      # narrower question the floor cannot - whether the setting *matches what
      # the job does* - by following each job's run blocks into the scripts
      # they call and looking for a push.
      - name: Every checkout says what happens to the job token
        run: node scripts/ci/check-checkout-credentials.mjs

      - name: Checkout-credential fixtures
        run: bash experiments/test-issue121-checkout-credentials.sh

  zizmor:
    name: zizmor
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-zizmor
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # A pull_request checkout is GitHub's merge preview, computed when the
      # pull request was last synchronised and never recomputed as main moves.
      # Merge the base branch first, so this job reports on what merging would
      # actually produce (issue #115, best practice #7).
      - name: Simulate a fresh merge with the base branch
        uses: ./.github/actions/simulate-fresh-merge

      # Both passes run through scripts/ci/run-zizmor.sh, which pins the image,
      # the floors and the scan targets in one place, and - the reason it
      # exists - hands zizmor a GitHub API token and fails the job if zizmor
      # says it is running offline anyway.
      #
      # Since 1.0 zizmor is offline unless it has a token, and `docker run`
      # forwards no environment, so the two invocations that used to live here
      # ran with the online audits switched off. The run on 1d9fb3e logged
      # `zizmor is running in offline mode by default; some audits and
      # auto-fixes will not be available` twice and reported no findings - about
      # a question it never asked, because `known-vulnerable-actions` needs the
      # GitHub Advisory Database (issue #123).
      #
      # GH_TOKEN, not GITHUB_TOKEN, because that is the name zizmor reads first
      # and the name the container is given. `contents: read` is all it needs;
      # the advisory data is public.
      - name: zizmor
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/run-zizmor.sh regular

      # The pass above runs zizmor's default `regular` persona, which is the
      # right default: `pedantic` surfaces hundreds of stylistic findings. But
      # the audits covering container image references — `unpinned-images`
      # among them — are Pedantic-only, so the `'*': hash-pin` policy declared
      # in .github/zizmor.yml was never enforced against `uses: docker://` or
      # `container:` at all: a policy the CI could not apply (issue #121).
      # Narrowing this second pass to high severity *and* high confidence
      # restores the enforcement without importing the noise. Measured: after
      # the digest pin above it reports nothing, and stays silent until someone
      # reintroduces a mutable image reference.
      - name: Audit for pedantic-only high-severity findings
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/run-zizmor.sh pedantic

  # === TERMINAL STATUS GATE ===
  #
  # The job that makes every other job's result reach the run's conclusion
  # (issue #121, reference-template best practice "every workflow gets a
  # terminal status gate").
  #
  # GitHub derives a run's conclusion from its jobs, and one cancellation
  # outranks any number of failures - so a run holding a failed job can still
  # come out grey, and everything that reads the run rather than each job (the
  # badge, `gh run list`, the run list quoted in issue #121 itself) reads that
  # as "no verdict" rather than "something broke". A gate's own conclusion is a
  # job conclusion, so when it errors the run is red no matter what else was
  # cancelled. The rationale, the measured run and the supersede-versus-overrun
  # rule are in scripts/ci/check-pipeline-status.sh.
  #
  # `!cancelled()`, not `always()`: cancelling a whole run is somebody's
  # decision and repainting it red would be a false positive, so this job is
  # skipped there. `cancelled()` is run-level, so a job cancelled on its own -
  # an overrun, or a per-job concurrency group firing - still reaches the gate.
  #
  # `needs` must name every other job in this file, or a job's result cannot
  # reach here at all. That is not left to review:
  # scripts/ci/check-status-gate-covers-all-jobs.mjs derives the list from this
  # workflow and fails when the two disagree.
  pipeline-status:
    name: pipeline-status
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [actionlint, zizmor]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Anonymous `git ls-remote` is enough to resolve the branch head, which is
      # how the script tells a superseded run from an overrun; no token is
      # persisted for it.
      - name: Check pipeline status
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-pipeline-status.sh
name: Dockerfiles

# Static checks over the Dockerfiles that define the boxes.
#
# Why this workflow exists (issue #115): this repository *is* a collection of
# Dockerfiles, and no linter had ever read one. actionlint reads the workflows,
# scripts.yml reads every *.sh, and the 23 Dockerfiles were the one body of
# source with no check at all. `apt install` instead of `apt-get install` was
# sitting in ubuntu/24.04/js/Dockerfile and in nine install scripts, printing
# "WARNING: apt does not have a stable CLI interface" into every box build -
# a warning nobody was looking for, because nothing collected it.

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      # A GitHub filter pattern is matched against the whole path from the
      # repository root, and `**/` requires a directory, so '**/Dockerfile'
      # does not match the root Dockerfile - the one this repository's own
      # image is built from (issue #121).
      - 'Dockerfile'
      - '**/Dockerfile'
      - '**/Dockerfile.*'
      - '**/*.Dockerfile'
      - '.hadolint.yaml'
      - 'scripts/ci/run-hadolint.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/dockerfiles.yml'
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      # A GitHub filter pattern is matched against the whole path from the
      # repository root, and `**/` requires a directory, so '**/Dockerfile'
      # does not match the root Dockerfile - the one this repository's own
      # image is built from (issue #121).
      - 'Dockerfile'
      - '**/Dockerfile'
      - '**/Dockerfile.*'
      - '**/*.Dockerfile'
      - '.hadolint.yaml'
      - 'scripts/ci/run-hadolint.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/dockerfiles.yml'

# Least-privilege default; this job only reads the checked-out tree.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:

  # `init.defaultBranch` answers it with a thirteen-line advice block - "Using
  # 'master' as the name for the initial branch... this default branch name will
  # change" - at the top of every job log. 19 checkouts in the runs issue #121
  # lists printed 247 lines of it, in jobs where nothing was wrong. No step can
  # fix it, because it is printed before the first step of ours runs; git reads
  # configuration from the environment too, and the environment is there from
  # the start. Ported from the js template, which carries the same three lines
  # with the same reasoning.
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

      cancel-in-progress: true

      - name: Checkout repository

          # widen what a compromised step could reach.

      # Merge the base branch first, so this job reports on what merging would
      # actually produce (issue #115, best practice #7).

  #
  # The job that makes every other job's result reach the run's conclusion
  # (issue #121, reference-template best practice "every workflow gets a
  # terminal status gate").
  #
  # GitHub derives a run's conclusion from its jobs, and one cancellation
  # outranks any number of failures - so a run holding a failed job can still
  # come out grey, and everything that reads the run rather than each job (the
  # badge, `gh run list`, the run list quoted in issue #121 itself) reads that
  # as "no verdict" rather than "something broke". A gate's own conclusion is a
  # job conclusion, so when it errors the run is red no matter what else was
  # cancelled. The rationale, the measured run and the supersede-versus-overrun
  # rule are in scripts/ci/check-pipeline-status.sh.
  #
  # `!cancelled()`, not `always()`: cancelling a whole run is somebody's
  # decision and repainting it red would be a false positive, so this job is
  # skipped there. `cancelled()` is run-level, so a job cancelled on its own -
  # an overrun, or a per-job concurrency group firing - still reaches the gate.
  #
  # `needs` must name every other job in this file, or a job's result cannot
  # reach here at all. That is not left to review:
  # scripts/ci/check-status-gate-covers-all-jobs.mjs derives the list from this
  # workflow and fails when the two disagree.
  pipeline-status:
    name: pipeline-status
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [hadolint]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Anonymous `git ls-remote` is enough to resolve the branch head, which is
      # how the script tells a superseded run from an overrun; no token is
      # persisted for it.
      - name: Check pipeline status
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-pipeline-status.sh
# lychee ignore patterns — regex matched against the URL.
#
# Ported from the reference template (issue #115, R5) and extended with the
# hosts this repository actually links to.
#
# Every entry is a false positive: a URL that is correct but that a link
# checker cannot verify - login-gated, rate-limited, bot-blocked, or served
# over TLS lychee will not negotiate. A URL that is genuinely broken belongs in
# the diff, not in this file; the first run of this gate found 111 of those and
# every one was fixed. Each pattern below carries the reason it is here.

# Localhost and local development URLs
http://localhost
https://localhost
http://127\.0\.0\.1
https://127\.0\.0\.1

# Example/placeholder URLs commonly used in documentation
https://example\.com
http://example\.com

# npmjs.com returns 403 to link checkers (bot protection)
https://www\.npmjs\.com

# medium.com returns 403 to link checkers (bot protection)
https://medium\.com

# web.archive.org returns 502 to link checkers (bot protection)
https://web\.archive\.org

# GitHub repository settings pages require admin authentication; an anonymous
# GET is 404 by design, for a URL the maintainer needs and that is correct.
https://github\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/settings/

# Docker Hub account settings redirect to the login flow, which lychee follows
# in a loop and rejects. Same reason as the GitHub settings pages above.
https://hub\.docker\.com/settings/

# manpages.ubuntu.com answers 503 under any load, and gnu.org rate-limits
# link checkers with 429. Both hosts are correct; their availability is not.
https://manpages\.ubuntu\.com
https://www\.gnu\.org

# packages.ubuntu.com takes 19-30s to answer, so lychee's 30s timeout trips on
# it often enough to fail the scheduled run on main. The pages are correct.
https://packages\.ubuntu\.com

# flatassembler.net offers no TLS suite lychee's rustls build will negotiate
# ("received fatal alert: HandshakeFailure"). The site is up in a browser.
https://(arm\.)?flatassembler\.net
# Changesets

This folder is used to track version changes using the changeset methodology.

## How to add a changeset

When you make changes that should trigger a version bump, create a new markdown file in this directory with the following format:

```markdown
---
bump: patch
---

Description of what changed
```

The `bump` field can be:
- `patch` - Bug fixes, minor updates (1.0.0 -> 1.0.1)
- `minor` - New features, backwards compatible (1.0.0 -> 1.1.0)
- `major` - Breaking changes (1.0.0 -> 2.0.0)

## How it works

1. Contributors add changeset files in their PRs
2. When merged to main, the CI workflow detects changesets
3. CI automatically bumps the VERSION file and creates a release
4. The changeset files are deleted after the version is applied

## File naming

Use descriptive names for changeset files, e.g.:
- `add-python-support.md`
- `fix-entrypoint-script.md`
- `update-nodejs-version.md`

Or use random names like: `happy-dogs-jump.md`

bc3cc33 2.10.0: Make every CI/CD check answer from the data it actually has (issue #123). The nine runs on `main` at `1d9fb3e` carry **804** lines matching `warn` or `error` and exactly **7** annotations; three of the seven said something untrue. **Eight of the nine runs were green**, and six of the twenty root causes are in those eight. One sentence covers all of them: a check that reported a verdict about data it never obtained. ### The red run was two false verdicts stacked `Measure Disk Space and Update README` annotated `…did not finish within its 2400s budget and was terminated` — and then ran **19 m 21 s** more, until `timeout-minutes: 60` cancelled it. `kill -0` exits 1 for both ESRCH ("gone") and EPERM ("alive, not yours to signal"), and the survivors were root-owned `apt-get` children of a `sudo`, so `run-with-budget-warning.sh` read them as finished, skipped its SIGKILL escalation, and exited 124 believing it had terminated the command. They also held the step's stdout, which is why the step could not end. Liveness now comes from the process table, escalation runs SIGTERM → SIGKILL → SIGKILL under `sudo`, any survivor is named in an `::error`, and the wrapper relays output instead of sharing a pipe. The gate then excused the cancellation as a supersede: `check-pipeline-status.sh` asked one question of the **run** and let the answer excuse every cancelled **job** in it, and `measure-disk-space.yml` declares `cancel-in-progress: false`, which a supersede cannot reach at all. `read-job-cancel-in-progress.sh` reads the effective value out of the workflow file `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF` names, and everything unreadable fails closed. Either verdict alone would have left a red run; together they produced a green one. ### The checks that could not fail zizmor printed `WARN audit: zizmor is running in offline mode` and `no findings to report` in the same green run: both passes were `docker run` without `-e GH_TOKEN`, so every online audit was skipped — `known-vulnerable-actions` among them, the one audit that can catch a supply-chain compromise of an action already trusted here. Measured over a `tj-actions/changed-files@v44` fixture: offline 7 findings, online 8, and the 2 `known-vulnerable-actions` hits appear only online. `run-zizmor.sh` pins image, floors and targets, passes the token by name and treats the offline banner as a failure. `if-no-files-found: warn` reported the absence of the only record of a run as a line in the log of the run whose record is missing; both uploads now ask `steps.<id>.outcome` and require files. `brew link … 2>&1 | grep -v Warning || true` tested grep's opinion of the text at four sites, hiding a failure that says why, a failure that says only `Warning:`, and issue #53's `timeout` 124. `npm --force` rode on the Playwright install since issue #84; twelve runs across both images, fresh and re-install, before and after `npm install -g npm@latest`, all exit 0 with the same version — the flag is gone. ### Text that was read as a verdict, and a log that was erased The runner's `ActionCommand.TryParse` accepts `##[` anywhere in a physical line, so `git commit` echoing a changeset that quotes `##[error]` becomes a `failure` annotation on a successful job. `run-with-commands-stopped.sh` brackets a child's output with `::stop-commands::<fresh 128-bit token>` and always resumes, at 15 call sites. Sweeping for those printers found `cmd 2>&1 | tee /dev/stderr`: `/dev/stderr` is `/proc/self/fd/2`, so `tee` **reopens** the file behind fd 2 with `O_TRUNC` — harmless when fd 2 is a pipe, destructive when it is a file. `capture-and-stream.sh` streams through a duplicate of the descriptor instead. ### `git diff` exiting 128 is not "nothing changed" Three release gates ran `git diff --name-only "origin/$BASE...HEAD"` and discarded the status: with no `fetch-depth: 0`, a renamed base or a failed fetch, the range does not resolve, the command prints nothing, and two of the three gates report the passing verdict on a branch that rewrote `VERSION` with no changeset. `scripts/release/pr-diff-range.sh` is the one place that asks what a pull request changed; it restores a base ref missing only locally and otherwise names the cause on stderr and returns 1. Extracting it surfaced that the changeset gate's path set omitted `VERSION`, `.github/actions/` and `.githooks/`, and echoed pull-request-controlled paths with command processing live. Two `gh` reads conflated "empty" with "failed"; the remaining **61** statements where a git or `gh` read could be mistaken for an answer — **27** in `scripts/`, `.github/` and `.githooks/` — are dispositioned one by one in `analysis/git-read-failure-sweep.md`, with the corrected query that finds them and the reason the first one could not. ### "Nothing to check" is not the same as "could not look" Eight `scripts/ci` gates discover their own inputs with `git ls-files`. Five ended that listing in `|| true` and the other three built it inside a process substitution; either way a git that could not answer — a busy index, an unreadable object, no `git` on `PATH` — arrived as an empty list, and the gate reported the empty list as a fact about the repository. Measured against the shipped `run-shellcheck.sh` with a `git` exiting 128: `==> No shell scripts to check`, status **0**, over 201 tracked shell scripts it never opened. All eight now separate "git could not answer" from "git answered, and there is nothing", and exit 2 naming which — as does `run-precommit-checks.sh`, the hook driver that runs them, which read the **index** the same way and printed `Nothing staged; no checks to run` over a commit it had not seen. The release path asked the same question of `VERSION`: 18 hand-rolled reads across six workflows, 16 of them behind `git pull origin main || true`, where an unreadable file leaves `version=` — a tag published as `ghcr.io/…/box-js:-amd64`, or a bump to `1.0.0` from whatever the version actually was. `scripts/release/release-version.sh` is the single reader now, it takes the version the pipeline already resolved (`fromJSON(inputs.changes)['version']`), and it refuses an empty one. The last one is a break this branch committed itself: three orphan `echo` lines left `release-full.yml` unparseable (`Psych::SyntaxError … line 175 column 33`), and all four gates that read workflow files exited 0 while describing its contents — each reads YAML with a regex or a `grep`, so a file that is not YAML at all is simply one they extract nothing from. `scripts/ci/check-workflow-yaml.sh` parses every workflow with a real parser before the others run. One step further out is the same question about a gate's *subject* rather than its input: `validate-changeset.sh` matched `.changeset/` at any depth, so this branch's own release run failed with `Invalid changeset format` over `dev/log/…/templates/go/.changeset/add-changeset-workflow.md` — a changeset belonging to another repository, pinned here as the evidence the issue asks for, written in the changesets format rather than this repository's `bump:` one. The pattern is anchored at the root now, at the consumer's depth, and every gate that discovers its own inputs was re-measured against an evidence tree that holds seven other projects' source — 1355 inputs across ten gates, none of them under `dev/log/`. ### The shell a runner hands you is not the shell you tested in `tr: write error: Broken pipe` and `grep: write error: Broken pipe` on two passing jobs: a step's shell starts with SIGPIPE `SIG_IGN` ([actions/runner#2684](https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/2684), open since 2023), an ignored disposition survives `exec`, and bash cannot reset one — so `producer | head` gets EPIPE, a stderr line, and under `pipefail` a non-zero pipeline. The eight runs the issue lists carried **98 annotations** — 58 `failure`, 29 `warning`, 11 `notice` — and seven of those eight runs were green. So any commit message quoting `##[error]` annotates the next release, and `stop-commands` is in the same registered set. `BUILDX_METADATA_PROVENANCE: disabled` at workflow scope in all six building workflows removes the payload rather than the printing. Filed as docker/buildx#4066, docker/build-push-action#1612 and actions/runner#4692, each with the reproduction, a workaround and a fix in diff form. ### The 28 warnings that were also a false negative `jlumbroso/free-disk-space` removes a fixed list of package names. Google publishes no arm64 apt repository, so on `ubuntu-24.04-arm` apt stops at `E: Unable to locate package google-chrome-stable`, exits 100 — and removes **none** of the other five in the same command. The annotation reported the absence of a package that architecture never had, and was simultaneously the only notice that every arm64 job was keeping the packages the reclaim existed to take. `scripts/ci/reclaim-large-packages.sh` hands apt the intersection of the action's own patterns with what `dpkg-query` reports installed, so a failure now means something installed could not be removed. ### The checks that could not fail `.hadolint.yaml` failed at `warning` while all ten findings in the repository are `info`, and the runner mapped annotation levels beside a threshold it never read. All ten are resolved — DL3015 per site, measured by resolving each apt plan twice in `ubuntu:24.04`, so `--no-install-recommends` is added where it is a no-op and refused where the recommends are the product — and the threshold is hadolint's default now. `zizmor` scanned `.github/workflows` and nothing else, so the four composite actions had never been read by any linter; widening it surfaced a High-confidence `template-injection` in `dockerhub-login`. The `'*': hash-pin` policy could not apply to images at all, because those audits are Pedantic-only: a second high/high pass restores it, and `docker://rhysd/actionlint` is pinned by digest — which then froze the wrong thing, because a digest pin freezes the check set and not just the binary. It checks the **index**, not the working tree, because `git commit` records the index and a hook that reads the worktree is wrong in both directions — passing a commit whose fix is unstaged, failing a commit whose breakage is unstaged. 42858af 2.8.0: Publish every architecture the release built, and fail when a tag serves fewer (issue #119). Run 34056619231 finished `success` and left `konard/box:latest` amd64-only — the tag the README hands to every reader, which had been multi-arch since June. `docker manifest inspect` still answered 200, so nothing noticed. Four mechanisms, one sentence: **"it resolves" is not "it was published"**. ### The two tools could never have agreed `mirror-to-dockerhub.sh` copies with `docker buildx imagetools create`, which always wraps its result in an OCI index — even around a single platform. `create-multiarch-manifest.sh` then fed those copies to `docker manifest create`, which refuses an index source: `docker.io/***/box:2.7.0-amd64 is a manifest list`, three times, 40 seconds, then a warning. Retrying a deterministic failure is not resilience, it is a permanent defect wearing a transient one's costume — which is why the warning read like a flaky registry for a month. The manifest step publishes with `imagetools create` now, and Docker Hub assembles nothing at all: it mirrors the index GHCR already serves, which is what the issue proposed. ### Which job may write a tag a user pulls The `box` amd64 job mirrored **8** tags, the four suffixed and the four unsuffixed, so an architecture-specific job claimed `:latest`; `box-dind`'s mirror wrote only suffixed tags, which is why `konard/box-dind:2.7.0` is simply absent. Two spellings of one step, disagreeing about a rule nobody had written down. It is written down now — only a manifest step may name a bare tag — and `experiments/test-issue119-tag-policy.sh` reads every image reference out of the five release workflows and asserts it, so the next family added to the matrix cannot pick the other convention. For the manifest step to be the only writer it has to know every tag the release writes, which it did not: `docker/metadata-action` evaluates `{{date 'YYYYMMDD'}}` when the step runs, and the full box takes over an hour to build, so the two architecture jobs of a release started near midnight UTC name different tags — and the date and commit tags stayed single-architecture (`ghcr.io/link-foundation/box:20260907 linux/amd64`). `scripts/release/image-tags.sh` computes the list once and hands it to the other jobs, so every tag of a release reaches the manifest step. ### The check now asks what a tag serves `check-publication.sh` asked whether a reference resolves, and an amd64-only index answers yes. It reads the platform list now and fails on a reference carrying less than the release built, holding three distinctions apart: a **missing** mirror tag is lag and stays a warning (a mirror may trail the registry of record), a mirror tag that **resolves with the wrong architectures** is an error because somebody pulling it today gets the wrong answer today, and an **unreadable** platform list means "I could not look" — never "one architecture", which would be issue #117's false claim pointed the other way, at the cost of a release. `EXPECTED_PLATFORMS` is a constant, so `PREVIOUS_VERSION` adds the comparison a constant cannot make: a tag that was multi-arch in the previous release and is single-arch now is a regression regardless. `latest` joined the sample, being the tag the regression landed on. ### The tables say what was measured The v2.7.0 notes listed `konard/box-dind:2.7.0` as not published and then linked its `2.7.0-arm64` tag, under a column headed **Multi-arch**, while `konard/box:2.7.0` served linux/amd64 alone. A heading reads the same in the release where it is false — the same defect as a check that cannot fail, in documentation form. The heading is "Tag", the cell carries the probe's answer for that exact reference (`**linux/amd64 only**, missing linux/arm64`), and a per-architecture tag is linked only where its parent index was measured to serve that platform. Without `VERIFY_IMAGES` nothing was measured and the notes say so instead of implying it. The README's tables follow, and now state what the registries actually carried on 2026-09-08. ### The two CI jobs that could not finish `pr-test / full` and `pr-test / dind-full` — the only two jobs that hold JS, essentials, 11 language images and the full box on one runner — died four times in the full box's `#64 exporting layers`, with `exit code 143` and `The runner has received a shutdown signal`, while every other job passed on the same commit. Nothing in either job had ever sampled a resource, so `scripts/ci/resource-monitor.sh` now prints memory, disk, swap and the biggest processes from *inside* the build step, which is the only output that survives a runner going down. It answered on the next run: 11 MB of disk consumed across the whole 4.5-minute export with 88 GB still free, against 2.3 GB → **18.8 GB of committed memory** still climbing when the runner was taken down. dockerd buffering an export in anonymous memory is [docker/buildx#1606](https://github.com/docker/buildx/issues/1606), open since Docker 23.0 with nothing to configure; what changed on our side is that commit 46f80a5 made the Lean boxes install a real toolchain, so the full box's `COPY --from=lean-stage` stopped copying a stub. 16 GB of RAM is what an `ubuntu-24.04` runner has and larger runners are not available here, so `scripts/ci/ensure-swap.sh` spends the idle disk on the resource that ran out: a 32 GB swap target, sized down only if it would encroach on the 40 GB the chain and its export still need, decided out loud on `[ensure-swap]` lines, and never a job failure — a runner that cannot get swap gets a warning and the build attempt, because the failure belongs on the build. The `full` dind variant gets 90 minutes instead of 60, since an export that pages is slower than one that does not, and a timeout would hide the fix. ### Evidence and tests Run anonymously against the released v2.7.0 from this branch, the new gate exits 1 with `::error title=The Docker Hub mirror of v2.7.0 is single-architecture` — GHCR 8/8 pullable and multi-arch, Docker Hub 5/8 with `konard/box:2.7.0` and `:latest` at the same amd64-only digest. The transcript, the regenerated notes and the per-reference platform sweeps are in `dev/log/issues/119/pulls/120/`; `docs/case-studies/issue-119/` has the full analysis. 170 offline assertions across seven suites: `test-issue115-release-notes.sh` (50), `test-issue119-ci-resource-headroom.sh` (40, with the swapfile's privileged steps stubbed so the sequence is checked without root), `test-issue119-platform-coverage.sh` (21), `test-issue119-image-tags.sh` (19), `test-issue119-check-publication.sh` (16), `test-issue119-tag-policy.sh` (13) and `test-issue119-manifest-media-type.sh` (11). ### Still outstanding Nothing here rewrites a tag that is already published, so the Docker Hub mirror of 2.7.0 stays wrong until a release runs with these changes. GHCR — the registry of record — has been correct throughout, including for the consumer that prompted the issue.

name: "Lychee Broken Link Checker"
description: "Quickly check links in Markdown, HTML, and text files"
inputs:
  args:
    description: "Lychee arguments (https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee#commandline-parameters)"
    default: "--verbose --no-progress './**/*.md' './**/*.html' './**/*.rst'"
    required: false
  debug:
    description: "Enable debug output in action (set -x). Helpful for troubleshooting."
    default: false
    required: false
  fail:
    description: "Fail entire pipeline on error (i.e. when lychee exit code is not 0)"
    default: true
    required: false
  failIfEmpty:
    description: "Fail entire pipeline if no links were found"
    default: true
    required: false
  format:
    description: "Summary output format (e.g. json)"
    default: "markdown"
    required: false
  jobSummary:
    description: "Write GitHub job summary at the end of the job (written on Markdown output only)"
    default: true
    required: false
  lycheeVersion:
    description: "Use custom version of lychee link checker"
    default: v0.24.2
    required: false
  output:
    description: "Summary output file path"
    default: "lychee/out.md"
    required: false
  checkbox:
    description: "Add Markdown Styled Checkboxes to the output"
    default: true
    required: false
  token:
    description: "Your GitHub Access Token, defaults to: {{ github.token }}"
    default: ${{ github.token }}
    required: false
  workingDirectory:
    description: "Directory to run lychee in"
    default: "."
    required: false
outputs:
  exit_code:
    description: "The exit code returned from Lychee"
    value: ${{ steps.run-lychee.outputs.exit_code }}
runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - name: Set up environment
      run: |
        # Install into $RUNNER_TEMP (not $HOME) so the install path is stable
        # across composite steps. On some runners $HOME is overridden per step
        # (e.g. actions/checkout temporarily sets it), which made the PATH
        # entry from one step and the install in another step diverge.
        echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee/bin"
      shell: bash
    - name: Download and extract lychee in temp directory
      id: lychee-setup
      run: |
        # Create a temporary directory for downloads and extraction
        TEMP_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/lychee-download"
        rm -rf "${TEMP_DIR}" && mkdir -p "${TEMP_DIR}"
        cd "${TEMP_DIR}"

        ARCH=$(uname -m)
        # Determine filename and download URL based on version
        if [[ "${LYCHEE_VERSION}" =~ ^v0\.0|^v0\.1[0-5]\. ]]; then
          FILENAME="lychee-${LYCHEE_VERSION}-${ARCH}-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
          DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/${LYCHEE_VERSION}/${FILENAME}"
        else
          FILENAME="lychee-${ARCH}-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
          if [[ "${LYCHEE_VERSION}" == 'nightly' ]]; then
            DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/nightly/${FILENAME}"
          elif [[ "${LYCHEE_VERSION}" == 'latest' ]]; then
            DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/latest/download/${FILENAME}"
          else
            DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-${LYCHEE_VERSION}/${FILENAME}"
          fi
        fi

        echo "Downloading from: ${DOWNLOAD_URL}"
        curl -sfLO "${DOWNLOAD_URL}"

bc3cc33 2.10.0: Make every CI/CD check answer from the data it actually has (issue #123). The nine runs on `main` at `1d9fb3e` carry **804** lines matching `warn` or `error` and exactly **7** annotations; three of the seven said something untrue. **Eight of the nine runs were green**, and six of the twenty root causes are in those eight. One sentence covers all of them: a check that reported a verdict about data it never obtained. ### The red run was two false verdicts stacked `Measure Disk Space and Update README` annotated `…did not finish within its 2400s budget and was terminated` — and then ran **19 m 21 s** more, until `timeout-minutes: 60` cancelled it. `kill -0` exits 1 for both ESRCH ("gone") and EPERM ("alive, not yours to signal"), and the survivors were root-owned `apt-get` children of a `sudo`, so `run-with-budget-warning.sh` read them as finished, skipped its SIGKILL escalation, and exited 124 believing it had terminated the command. They also held the step's stdout, which is why the step could not end. Liveness now comes from the process table, escalation runs SIGTERM → SIGKILL → SIGKILL under `sudo`, any survivor is named in an `::error`, and the wrapper relays output instead of sharing a pipe. The gate then excused the cancellation as a supersede: `check-pipeline-status.sh` asked one question of the **run** and let the answer excuse every cancelled **job** in it, and `measure-disk-space.yml` declares `cancel-in-progress: false`, which a supersede cannot reach at all. `read-job-cancel-in-progress.sh` reads the effective value out of the workflow file `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF` names, and everything unreadable fails closed. Either verdict alone would have left a red run; together they produced a green one. ### The checks that could not fail zizmor printed `WARN audit: zizmor is running in offline mode` and `no findings to report` in the same green run: both passes were `docker run` without `-e GH_TOKEN`, so every online audit was skipped — `known-vulnerable-actions` among them, the one audit that can catch a supply-chain compromise of an action already trusted here. Measured over a `tj-actions/changed-files@v44` fixture: offline 7 findings, online 8, and the 2 `known-vulnerable-actions` hits appear only online. `run-zizmor.sh` pins image, floors and targets, passes the token by name and treats the offline banner as a failure. `if-no-files-found: warn` reported the absence of the only record of a run as a line in the log of the run whose record is missing; both uploads now ask `steps.<id>.outcome` and require files. `brew link … 2>&1 | grep -v Warning || true` tested grep's opinion of the text at four sites, hiding a failure that says why, a failure that says only `Warning:`, and issue #53's `timeout` 124. `npm --force` rode on the Playwright install since issue #84; twelve runs across both images, fresh and re-install, before and after `npm install -g npm@latest`, all exit 0 with the same version — the flag is gone. ### Text that was read as a verdict, and a log that was erased The runner's `ActionCommand.TryParse` accepts `##[` anywhere in a physical line, so `git commit` echoing a changeset that quotes `##[error]` becomes a `failure` annotation on a successful job. `run-with-commands-stopped.sh` brackets a child's output with `::stop-commands::<fresh 128-bit token>` and always resumes, at 15 call sites. Sweeping for those printers found `cmd 2>&1 | tee /dev/stderr`: `/dev/stderr` is `/proc/self/fd/2`, so `tee` **reopens** the file behind fd 2 with `O_TRUNC` — harmless when fd 2 is a pipe, destructive when it is a file. `capture-and-stream.sh` streams through a duplicate of the descriptor instead. ### `git diff` exiting 128 is not "nothing changed" Three release gates ran `git diff --name-only "origin/$BASE...HEAD"` and discarded the status: with no `fetch-depth: 0`, a renamed base or a failed fetch, the range does not resolve, the command prints nothing, and two of the three gates report the passing verdict on a branch that rewrote `VERSION` with no changeset. `scripts/release/pr-diff-range.sh` is the one place that asks what a pull request changed; it restores a base ref missing only locally and otherwise names the cause on stderr and returns 1. Extracting it surfaced that the changeset gate's path set omitted `VERSION`, `.github/actions/` and `.githooks/`, and echoed pull-request-controlled paths with command processing live. Two `gh` reads conflated "empty" with "failed"; the remaining **61** statements where a git or `gh` read could be mistaken for an answer — **27** in `scripts/`, `.github/` and `.githooks/` — are dispositioned one by one in `analysis/git-read-failure-sweep.md`, with the corrected query that finds them and the reason the first one could not. ### "Nothing to check" is not the same as "could not look" Eight `scripts/ci` gates discover their own inputs with `git ls-files`. Five ended that listing in `|| true` and the other three built it inside a process substitution; either way a git that could not answer — a busy index, an unreadable object, no `git` on `PATH` — arrived as an empty list, and the gate reported the empty list as a fact about the repository. Measured against the shipped `run-shellcheck.sh` with a `git` exiting 128: `==> No shell scripts to check`, status **0**, over 201 tracked shell scripts it never opened. All eight now separate "git could not answer" from "git answered, and there is nothing", and exit 2 naming which — as does `run-precommit-checks.sh`, the hook driver that runs them, which read the **index** the same way and printed `Nothing staged; no checks to run` over a commit it had not seen. The release path asked the same question of `VERSION`: 18 hand-rolled reads across six workflows, 16 of them behind `git pull origin main || true`, where an unreadable file leaves `version=` — a tag published as `ghcr.io/…/box-js:-amd64`, or a bump to `1.0.0` from whatever the version actually was. `scripts/release/release-version.sh` is the single reader now, it takes the version the pipeline already resolved (`fromJSON(inputs.changes)['version']`), and it refuses an empty one.     steps:

      # A pull_request checkout is GitHub's merge preview, computed when the
      # pull request was last synchronised and never recomputed as main moves.
      # Merge the base branch first, so this job reports on what merging would
      # actually produce (issue #115, best practice #7).
      - name: Simulate a fresh merge with the base branch
        uses: ./.github/actions/simulate-fresh-merge

      # A `uses:` step takes the budget GitHub applies to a whole step, since it
      # cannot be routed through scripts/ci/run-with-budget-warning.sh (issue
      # #121, docs/CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md). The slowest run measured took 30
      # seconds; 5 minutes bounds a slow external host without waiting for the
      # job cap, which would report the job *cancelled* and skip the reporting
      # steps below - including the recovery pass that tells a false positive
      # from a real broken link.
      #
      # --include-fragments: without it lychee resolves a link's *document* and
      # stops, so `docs/RELEASING.md#making-the-ghcr-packages-public` passes as
      # long as the file exists, whatever the headings inside it say - and an
      # anchor is exactly the part of a link that a heading rename breaks. This
      # gate had never checked one (issue #121). Measured on this tree: a
      # fixture that renames the target heading of a same-file and a cross-file
      # anchor passes without the flag and fails with it; over the whole corpus
      # the flag reports 681 links, 473 unique, 667 OK, 0 errors in 14.6s, after
      # the three genuinely dead remote anchors it found were fixed (docker's
      # #entrypoint-default-command-to-execute-at-runtime, jpetazzo/dind's
      # #warning-..., and a GitHub docs page that moved). Evidence:
      # dev/log/issues/121/pulls/122/doc-fragments/. It applies to remote
      # anchors too, which is why the number of requests does not change: lychee
      # already fetched those pages, it just discarded their ids.
      - name: Check links with lychee
        id: lychee
        timeout-minutes: 5
        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
        with:
          args: >-
            --no-progress
            ${{ inputs.verbose && '--verbose' || '' }}
            --cache
            --max-cache-age 1d
            --include-fragments
            --max-retries 2
            --timeout 30
            --exclude-path dev/log
            './**/*.md'
          # Not a failure yet: a broken link that the Wayback Machine has
          # archived gets a concrete replacement suggested below, which is more
          # use to the author than a bare red X.
          fail: false
          lycheeVersion: v0.24.2
          output: lychee/out.md
          jobSummary: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Set up Node
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code == '2'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # lychee classifies an error by the phase it happened in, and a failure
      # during connect is never retried - `--max-retries` does not apply to it
      # (lycheeverse/lychee#2297). So a healthy host that answers one TCP reset,
      # which a CI address range collects from rate-limiting and load-shedding
      # hosts, is reported broken without a single retry and fails this gate:
      # a false positive (issue #121). Ask those URLs again, outside lychee. A
      # temporary HTTP error (408, 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504) can also recover:
      # PR #132 failed on two healthy GitHub docs links answering 503. Retry
      # those within the same wall-clock budget; only an accepted status can
      # recover them. Permanent failures such as 404 remain final. URLs with
      # fragments stay final because an HTTP status cannot check anchors.
      - name: Re-check unanswered links and temporary HTTP errors
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code == '2'
        id: recheck
        run: node scripts/ci/recheck-broken-links.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
          RECOVERED_OUTPUT: lychee/recovered.txt
          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}
          BOX_VERBOSE: ${{ inputs.verbose && '1' || '0' }}

      # `!= 'true'`, never `== 'false'`: a skipped or crashed re-check leaves
      # the output empty, and only the `!=` form reads that as "still failing".
      - name: Look for Web Archive replacements
        continue-on-error: true
        if: >-
          steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code == '2' &&
          steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true'
        run: node scripts/ci/check-web-archive.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
          RECOVERED_URLS: lychee/recovered.txt

      - name: Report a link checker execution failure
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && steps.lychee.outcome != '' && steps.lychee.outcome != 'skipped' &&
          steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0' && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '2' }}
        env:
          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}
        run: |
          echo "::error title=links::Lychee did not complete a link scan (exit: ${LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE:-unavailable})."
          exit 1

      - name: Fail if broken links were found
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code == '2' &&
          steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error title=links::lychee found broken links."
          echo
          echo "An archive URL is a suggested replacement; it does not make the"
          echo "live link valid. For each broken link, in order of preference:"
          echo "  1. Point at the current location of the same content."
          echo "  2. Point at the archive.org snapshot suggested above."
          echo "  3. Pin a GitHub link to the commit that still holds the file."
          echo "  4. Delete the link if the content is gone and not worth citing."
          echo "  5. Add the URL to .lycheeignore *with a reason* - but only if"
          echo "     the link is correct and merely unverifiable (login-gated,"
          echo "     rate-limited, bot-blocked). A dead link is not a false"
          echo "     positive, and silencing it is the defect issue #115 is about."
          echo

      # A pull_request checkout is GitHub's merge preview, computed when the
      # pull request was last synchronised and never recomputed as main moves.
      # Merge the base branch first, so this job reports on what merging would
      # actually produce (issue #115, best practice #7).
      - name: Simulate a fresh merge with the base branch
        uses: ./.github/actions/simulate-fresh-merge

      # A `uses:` step takes the budget GitHub applies to a whole step, since it
      # cannot be routed through scripts/ci/run-with-budget-warning.sh (issue
      # #121, docs/CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md). The slowest run measured took 30
      # seconds; 5 minutes bounds a slow external host without waiting for the
      # job cap, which would report the job *cancelled* and skip the reporting
      # steps below - including the recovery pass that tells a false positive
      # from a real broken link.
      #
      # --include-fragments: without it lychee resolves a link's *document* and
      # stops, so `docs/RELEASING.md#making-the-ghcr-packages-public` passes as
      # long as the file exists, whatever the headings inside it say - and an
      # anchor is exactly the part of a link that a heading rename breaks. This
      # gate had never checked one (issue #121). Measured on this tree: a
      # fixture that renames the target heading of a same-file and a cross-file
      # anchor passes without the flag and fails with it; over the whole corpus
      # the flag reports 681 links, 473 unique, 667 OK, 0 errors in 14.6s, after
      # the three genuinely dead remote anchors it found were fixed (docker's
      # #entrypoint-default-command-to-execute-at-runtime, jpetazzo/dind's
      # #warning-..., and a GitHub docs page that moved). Evidence:
      # dev/log/issues/121/pulls/122/doc-fragments/. It applies to remote
      # anchors too, which is why the number of requests does not change: lychee
      # already fetched those pages, it just discarded their ids.
      - name: Check links with lychee
        id: lychee
        timeout-minutes: 5
        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
        with:
          args: >-
            --no-progress
            ${{ inputs.verbose && '--verbose' || '' }}
            --cache
            --max-cache-age 1d
            --include-fragments
            --max-retries 2
            --timeout 30
            --exclude-path dev/log
            './**/*.md'
          # Not a failure yet: a broken link that the Wayback Machine has
          # archived gets a concrete replacement suggested below, which is more
          # use to the author than a bare red X.
          fail: false
          lycheeVersion: v0.24.2
          output: lychee/out.md
          jobSummary: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Set up Node
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code == '2'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # lychee classifies an error by the phase it happened in, and a failure
      # during connect is never retried - `--max-retries` does not apply to it
      # (lycheeverse/lychee#2297). So a healthy host that answers one TCP reset,
      # which a CI address range collects from rate-limiting and load-shedding
      # hosts, is reported broken without a single retry and fails this gate:
      # a false positive (issue #121). Ask those URLs again, outside lychee. A
      # temporary HTTP error (408, 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504) can also recover:
      # PR #132 failed on two healthy GitHub docs links answering 503. Retry
      # those within the same wall-clock budget; only an accepted status can
      # recover them. Permanent failures such as 404 remain final. URLs with
      # fragments stay final because an HTTP status cannot check anchors.
      - name: Re-check unanswered links and temporary HTTP errors
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code == '2'
        id: recheck
        run: node scripts/ci/recheck-broken-links.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
          RECOVERED_OUTPUT: lychee/recovered.txt
          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}
          BOX_VERBOSE: ${{ inputs.verbose && '1' || '0' }}

      # `!= 'true'`, never `== 'false'`: a skipped or crashed re-check leaves
      # the output empty, and only the `!=` form reads that as "still failing".
      - name: Look for Web Archive replacements
        continue-on-error: true
        if: >-
          steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code == '2' &&
          steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true'
        run: node scripts/ci/check-web-archive.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
          RECOVERED_URLS: lychee/recovered.txt

      - name: Report a link checker execution failure
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && steps.lychee.outcome != '' && steps.lychee.outcome != 'skipped' &&
          steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0' && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '2' }}
        env:
          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}
        run: |
          echo "::error title=links::Lychee did not complete a link scan (exit: ${LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE:-unavailable})."
          exit 1

      - name: Fail if broken links were found
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code == '2' &&
          steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error title=links::lychee found broken links."
          echo
          echo "An archive URL is a suggested replacement; it does not make the"
          echo "live link valid. For each broken link, in order of preference:"
          echo "  1. Point at the current location of the same content."
          echo "  2. Point at the archive.org snapshot suggested above."
          echo "  3. Pin a GitHub link to the commit that still holds the file."
          echo "  4. Delete the link if the content is gone and not worth citing."
          echo "  5. Add the URL to .lycheeignore *with a reason* - but only if"
          echo "     the link is correct and merely unverifiable (login-gated,"
          echo "     rate-limited, bot-blocked). A dead link is not a false"
          echo "     positive, and silencing it is the defect issue #115 is about."
          echo

  cat >"$FRAG_DIR/b.md" <<'MD'

  frag_run() {

      --no-progress --offline "$@" './**/*.md' 2>&1
  }

  # Intact: the same-file heading exists, so both anchors resolve.
  printf '\n## The Section\n' >>"$FRAG_DIR/a.md"
  if frag_run --include-fragments | grep -q '0 Errors'; then
    pass "with the flag, anchors that resolve are reported OK (no false positive)"
  else
    fail "with the flag, valid anchors are reported broken"
  fi

  # Rename both targets: one same-file anchor, one cross-file anchor.
  sed -i 's/## The Section/## Renamed Section/' "$FRAG_DIR/a.md"
  sed -i 's/## Other Heading/## Renamed Other/' "$FRAG_DIR/b.md"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test-issue115-links-gate.sh
#
# Issue #115, best practice #12 (documentation validation). Pins the link
# checker and, more importantly, the policy that keeps it honest.
#
# Nothing in this repository had ever resolved a URL. The first lychee run over
# the tracked markdown reported 113 failures over 16 files - 107 distinct URLs:
# case studies citing CI logs GitHub had already deleted (90-day retention), 85
# README links to GHCR packages that were never published, an OWASP page that
# 404s, a GitHub repository that had been transferred. Every one of them was
# fixed in the diff. The failure mode this suite exists to prevent is the cheap
# alternative - moving a dead link into .lycheeignore, which turns a real
# finding into permanent silence.
#
# So the assertions are of two kinds:
#   1. the gate exists, is wired to files that exist, and reports a failure
#      rather than a green tick (lychee's own `fail: false` + an explicit step);
#   2. .lycheeignore silences only URLs that are correct-but-unverifiable, and
#      no pattern in it is broad enough to cover a URL this repository relies
#      on being right.
#
# Static assertions plus offline unit tests of the Wayback parser. Set
# LINKS_LIVE=1 to also run lychee for real (needs docker + network).
#
# Usage: bash experiments/test-issue115-links-gate.sh

set -uo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." || exit 1

IGNORE=".lycheeignore"
# The image the workflow's comments tell a reader to reproduce with; the
# fixtures below use the same one so "it passes locally" means the same thing.
LYCHEE_IMAGE="lycheeverse/lychee:0.24.2"
WORKFLOW=".github/workflows/links.yml"
echo
echo "== Part 5: the workflow reads the output so that a skip fails safe =="

assert_workflow() {
  if grep -qF -- "$2" "$WORKFLOW"; then
    pass "$1"
  else
    fail "$1" "not found in $WORKFLOW: $2"
  fi
}

assert_workflow "the re-check step runs the script" \
  "run: node scripts/ci/recheck-broken-links.mjs"
assert_workflow "the re-check step is addressable as steps.recheck" \
  "id: recheck"
assert_workflow "the re-check only runs when lychee failed" \
  "if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0"
assert_workflow "the recovered list is handed to the Wayback step" \
  "RECOVERED_URLS: lychee/recovered.txt"
assert_workflow "the re-check writes the list the Wayback step reads" \
  "RECOVERED_OUTPUT: lychee/recovered.txt"

# `== 'false'` is the form that fails open: a skipped step leaves the output
# empty, which is neither 'true' nor 'false', so the consumer would skip too.
consumers="$(grep -c "all_recovered != 'true'" "$WORKFLOW")"
if [ "$consumers" -ge 2 ]; then
  pass "both consumers read all_recovered with != 'true' ($consumers)"
else
  fail "expected the Wayback step and the failing step to read all_recovered with != 'true'" \
    "found $consumers"
fi
if grep -q "all_recovered == 'false'" "$WORKFLOW"; then
  fail "a consumer reads all_recovered with == 'false', which fails open on a skipped step"
else
  pass "no consumer reads all_recovered with == 'false'"
fi
if grep -q "steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true'" "$WORKFLOW" \
  && grep -q '!cancelled() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0' "$WORKFLOW"; then
  pass "the failing step still runs on its own when the re-check recovered nothing"
else
  fail "the failing step's condition no longer names both lychee and the re-check"
fi

 * @param {string} content - The markdown content from lychee

  const entryPattern =
    /^[ \t]*(?:\*|-)[ \t]+\[([^\]]+)\][ \t]+<?([^\s>|)]+)>?(?:[ \t]+\(at [^)]*\))?[ \t]*\|?[ \t]*([^\r\n]*)$/gim;

  # repository. Monday 06:00 UTC, same slot the template uses.
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least-privilege default; the CodeQL job escalates on its own.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # actions/checkout's first act is `git init`, and a git with no configured
  # `init.defaultBranch` answers it with a thirteen-line advice block - "Using
  # 'master' as the name for the initial branch... this default branch name will
  # change" - at the top of every job log. 19 checkouts in the runs issue #121
  # lists printed 247 lines of it, in jobs where nothing was wrong. No step can
  # fix it, because it is printed before the first step of ours runs; git reads
  # configuration from the environment too, and the environment is there from
  # the start. Ported from the js template, which carries the same three lines
  # with the same reasoning.
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  codeql:
    name: security / CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
  log "=== Changed files (classified for build decision) ==="
  if [ -z "$changed_files" ]; then
    log "  (none)"
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | sed 's/^/  /'
  fi
  log ""

  # --- Top-level categories ---
  local docker scripts ubuntu workflow version
  docker=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^Dockerfile$')
  scripts=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^scripts/')
  ubuntu=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^ubuntu/')
  workflow=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^\.github/(workflows|actions)/')
  version=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^VERSION$')
  set_output docker "$docker"
  set_output scripts "$scripts"
  set_output ubuntu "$ubuntu"
  set_output workflow "$workflow"
  set_output version "$version"

  # --- Per-image categories ---
  local js essentials full common dind
  js=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^ubuntu/24\.04/js/')
  essentials=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^ubuntu/24\.04/essentials-box/')
  full=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^(ubuntu/24\.04/full-box/|Dockerfile$|scripts/)')
  common=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^ubuntu/24\.04/common\.sh$')
  # dind: image source and the CI example tests that exercise it. Documentation
  # under docs/dind/ is intentionally NOT a build trigger (issue #108: docs and
  # other non-essential files must not run the image build/test matrix).
  dind=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^(ubuntu/24\.04/dind/|tests/dind/)')
  set_output js "$js"
  set_output essentials "$essentials"
  set_output full "$full"
  set_output common "$common"
  set_output dind "$dind"

  # --- Per-language categories ---
  local lang val
  for lang in $LANGUAGES; do
    val=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches "^ubuntu/24\\.04/${lang}/")
    set_output "$lang" "$val"
  done

  # --- Aggregate build decision ---
  local should_build="false" reason="no relevant changes detected"
  if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME:-}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="manual dispatch"
  elif [ "$docker" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="Dockerfile changes"
  elif [ "$scripts" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="scripts changes"
  elif [ "$ubuntu" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="ubuntu modular scripts changes"
  elif [ "$workflow" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="workflow/action changes"
  elif [ "$version" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="VERSION file changes"
  elif [ "$dind" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="dind image/test changes"
  fi
  set_output should-build "$should_build"
  log ""
  if [ "$should_build" = "true" ]; then
    log "Build needed: ${reason}"
  else
    log "No build needed: ${reason}"
  fi
}

main "$@"
