  # with the same reasoning.
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  codeql:
    name: security / CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
  log "=== Changed files (classified for build decision) ==="
  if [ -z "$changed_files" ]; then
    log "  (none)"
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | sed 's/^/  /'
  fi
  log ""

  # --- Top-level categories ---
  local docker scripts ubuntu workflow version
  docker=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^Dockerfile$')
  scripts=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^scripts/')
  ubuntu=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^ubuntu/')
  workflow=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^\.github/(workflows|actions)/')
  version=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^VERSION$')
  set_output docker "$docker"
  set_output scripts "$scripts"
  set_output ubuntu "$ubuntu"
  set_output workflow "$workflow"
  set_output version "$version"

  # --- Per-image categories ---
  local js essentials full common dind
  js=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^ubuntu/24\.04/js/')
  essentials=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^ubuntu/24\.04/essentials-box/')
  full=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^(ubuntu/24\.04/full-box/|Dockerfile$|scripts/)')
  common=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^ubuntu/24\.04/common\.sh$')
  # dind: image source and the CI example tests that exercise it. Documentation
  # under docs/dind/ is intentionally NOT a build trigger (issue #108: docs and
  # other non-essential files must not run the image build/test matrix).
  dind=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches '^(ubuntu/24\.04/dind/|tests/dind/)')
  set_output js "$js"
  set_output essentials "$essentials"
  set_output full "$full"
  set_output common "$common"
  set_output dind "$dind"

  # --- Per-language categories ---
  local lang val
  for lang in $LANGUAGES; do
    val=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | matches "^ubuntu/24\\.04/${lang}/")
    set_output "$lang" "$val"
  done

  # --- Aggregate build decision ---
  local should_build="false" reason="no relevant changes detected"
  if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME:-}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="manual dispatch"
  elif [ "$docker" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="Dockerfile changes"
  elif [ "$scripts" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="scripts changes"
  elif [ "$ubuntu" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="ubuntu modular scripts changes"
  elif [ "$workflow" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="workflow/action changes"
  elif [ "$version" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="VERSION file changes"
  elif [ "$dind" = "true" ]; then
    should_build="true"
    reason="dind image/test changes"
  fi
  set_output should-build "$should_build"
  log ""
  if [ "$should_build" = "true" ]; then
    log "Build needed: ${reason}"
  else
    log "No build needed: ${reason}"
  fi
}

main "$@"

cat >/tmp/box-135-head-report.md <<'EOF'
Link recovery can mark a missing page healthy when HEAD returns 200 and GET returns 404. Lychee defaults to GET, so recovery needs the same HTTP method. This was found while comparing the reference templates for [Box issue #135](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/issues/135).

## Reproduce

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace LinkFoundation\Template\Pipeline;

/**
 * Tiny HTTP client used to probe the Packagist registry.
 *
 * Network access is wrapped behind a swappable fetcher callable so tests can
 * inject canned responses without hitting the network.
 *
 * @phpstan-type Fetcher callable(string, string, array<string, string>): array{status:int, body:string}
 */
final class Http
{
    /** @var callable(string, string, array<string, string>): array{status:int, body:string} */
    private $fetcher;

    /**
     * @param (callable(string, string, array<string, string>): array{status:int, body:string})|null $fetcher
     */
    public function __construct(?callable $fetcher = null)
    {
        $this->fetcher = $fetcher ?? self::defaultFetcher();
    }

    /**
     * @param array<string, string> $headers
     * @return array{status:int, body:string}
     */
    public function get(string $url, array $headers = []): array
    {
        return ($this->fetcher)('GET', $url, $headers);
    }

    /**
     * @param array<string, string> $headers
     * @return array{status:int, body:string}
     */
    public function head(string $url, array $headers = []): array
    {
        return ($this->fetcher)('HEAD', $url, $headers);
    }

    /**
     * @return callable(string, string, array<string, string>): array{status:int, body:string}
     */
    private static function defaultFetcher(): callable
    {
        return static function (string $method, string $url, array $headers = []): array {
            $headerLines = ['User-Agent: php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template'];
            foreach ($headers as $name => $value) {
                $headerLines[] = "{$name}: {$value}";
            }

            $context = stream_context_create([
                'http' => [
                    'method' => $method,
                    'timeout' => 30,
                    'ignore_errors' => true,
                    'header' => implode("\r\n", $headerLines),
                ],
            ]);

            // Do not reuse a previous response when this request cannot connect.
            http_clear_last_response_headers();
            $body = @file_get_contents($url, false, $context);
            $status = self::statusFromHeaders(http_get_last_response_headers() ?? []);

            return ['status' => $status, 'body' => $body === false ? '' : $body];
        };
    }

    /**
     * @param list<string> $headers
     */
    private static function statusFromHeaders(array $headers): int
    {
        foreach ($headers as $header) {
            if (preg_match('#^HTTP/\S+\s+(\d+)#', $header, $m)) {
                return (int) $m[1];
            }
        }

        return 0;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace LinkFoundation\Template\Pipeline;

/**
 * Tiny HTTP client used to probe the Packagist registry.
 *
 * Network access is wrapped behind a swappable fetcher callable so tests can
 * inject canned responses without hitting the network.
 *
 * @phpstan-type Fetcher callable(string, string, array<string, string>): array{status:int, body:string}
 */
final class Http
{
    /** @var callable(string, string, array<string, string>): array{status:int, body:string} */
    private $fetcher;

    /**
     * @param (callable(string, string, array<string, string>): array{status:int, body:string})|null $fetcher
     */
    public function __construct(?callable $fetcher = null)
    {
        $this->fetcher = $fetcher ?? self::defaultFetcher();
    }

    /**
     * @param array<string, string> $headers
     * @return array{status:int, body:string}
     */
    public function get(string $url, array $headers = []): array
    {
        return ($this->fetcher)('GET', $url, $headers);
    }

    /**
     * @param array<string, string> $headers
     * @return array{status:int, body:string}
     */
    public function head(string $url, array $headers = []): array
    {
        return ($this->fetcher)('HEAD', $url, $headers);
    }

    /**
     * @return callable(string, string, array<string, string>): array{status:int, body:string}
     */
    private static function defaultFetcher(): callable
    {
        return static function (string $method, string $url, array $headers = []): array {
            $headerLines = ['User-Agent: php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template'];
            foreach ($headers as $name => $value) {
                $headerLines[] = "{$name}: {$value}";
            }

            $context = stream_context_create([
                'http' => [
                    'method' => $method,
                    'timeout' => 30,
                    'ignore_errors' => true,
                    'header' => implode("\r\n", $headerLines),
                ],
            ]);

            // Do not reuse a previous response when this request cannot connect.
            http_clear_last_response_headers();
            $body = @file_get_contents($url, false, $context);
            $status = self::statusFromHeaders(http_get_last_response_headers() ?? []);

            return ['status' => $status, 'body' => $body === false ? '' : $body];
        };
    }

    /**
     * @param list<string> $headers
     */
    private static function statusFromHeaders(array $headers): int
    {
        foreach ($headers as $header) {
            if (preg_match('#^HTTP/\S+\s+(\d+)#', $header, $m)) {
                return (int) $m[1];
            }
        }

        return 0;
    }
}

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

content.text:
You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share a workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely achieved.

# Completing the user's task

Persist until you've completed the task the user asked for. Avoid stopping to end the turn while the task is incomplete or if there is an authorized next step you can take, and instead take the next steps within task scope to progress the user's request. Make sure that you have accounted for every part of the user's request, and persist until you've delivered a result that fully satisfies the user's goal. Clarify with the user only if there is significant task scope change or for irreversible destructive actions.

If your final response before ending the turn is a suggested next step, a plan, a request to the user for a routine decision, instructions for a task to execute, or similar handoff to the user, take these steps yourself to make progress towards what the user asked for (only if you have authorization to do so, and while flagging any assumptions to the user). Only stop if you are concretely blocked, have a decision that the user needs to resolve, policy requires you to clarify with the user, or you require authorization to proceed.

# Personality

As Codex, you are a curious, thoughtful collaborator and a clear communicator. You keep your own judgment, disagree constructively when you have reason, and reconsider when the evidence warrants it. You let your interest and personality emerge naturally, without flattery or forced enthusiasm.

## Writing style

Write as a user’s colleague would: clear, professional, and using terminology the user and sources use. Keep technical details and use domain-specific language when they make the explanation more precise. Use the active voice and keep closely related details together. Cover the key points up front, and avoid references that the reader can only make sense of later in the response. Give the user enough context to follow your reasoning. 

Do not invent jargon, new terms, or metaphors. Use established names or a short explanation instead. Do not invent shorthand naming, internal implementation labels, and unnecessary process narration.

Do not repeat a previous point or insight with a declarative sentence. Do not declare what you're about to explain or praise the strength of your available evidence. Never announce that a finding or explanation is useful, compelling, or well supported. Don't use lead-in phrases or sentences that label a paragraph or announce your next point. Each sentence should progress the user's task. Do not use slogan-like summaries, and prefer concrete explanations instead.

Do not provide unsolicited recommendations or invent concerns or misconceptions unless explicitly called for. Do not provide preemptive disclaimers, e.g. "this doesn't mean...", "the key is...", "this is why I...".

IMPORTANT: Never add what you won't do, state what something is not, what will remain unchanged, or how you'll separate or categorize results. NEVER use contrastive framing such as "X, not Y", "These are X, not Y", "I'll do X rather than Y", "it is about X, not about Y", and "X—not Y". Do not compare to an unsolicited alternative that the user did not directly ask about. Avoid invented compound labels like "exact-head checks" and "editorial-row layouts", vague qualifiers, and canned transitions. Carefully follow these instructions when writing in documents, slides or other artifacts as well.

In prose, do not use semicolons. Do not use colons to introduce explanations or examples, including after list labels. Avoid replacing colons directly with a period, instead rephrase the thought. 

Avoid apologies and self-blame. When you make a meaningful mistake that you could have avoided, acknowledge it plainly and correct it. Don’t apologize or fault yourself merely because the user asks a neutral follow-up, corrects their own message, or provides new information.

Place source links at the end of each bullet or paragraph and keep explanatory text and prose free of inline links unless absolutely necessary.

## Intermediate commentary

Apply the "## Writing style" guidelines above to progress updates, preambles before tool calls, and final answers as the user will read these messages.

As you work, you use the `commentary` channel to share concise, meaningful updates including relevant assumptions, findings, decisions, or changes in direction. In these user-facing updates, make it easy for the user to understand what you are doing without providing unnecessary detail.

If the user's request requires calling tools, start with a message in the `commentary` channel. Prefer sending consistent, frequent communication to the user during your turn. When the user asks you to wait or monitor through completion or if it's needed for a longer horizon task, you can sleep for as long as is required (generally 60 seconds by default) between checks.

Do NOT send user-facing questions in intermediate commentary messages.

## Final answer

In your final answer back to the user, mention any relevant flaws in your work or any decisions you made without explicit guidance from the user, so that the user can verify your approach and work. Disclosure in commentary alone is not enough. You MUST repeat any such disclosures in the final answer.

Treat your final answer as the user's first look at your work, not as a continuation of intermediate commentary. The final answer must always be fully self-contained: users should never need to read earlier commentary updates for context, since they are collapsed when the final answer is shown to the user. 

Write the final answer and all other human-facing material anew for the intended reader. Do not copy or closely paraphrase your reasoning or adopt its writing style. ){"body":"## Problem

`.github/workflows/links.yml` reports success when Lychee finds broken live links if every broken URL has a Wayback snapshot. The repository still contains and serves broken links; the Python helper only prints suggested replacements and does not rewrite them.

Current terminal condition:

```yaml
if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0 && steps.webarchive.outputs.all_archived != 'true'
```

This makes an archived-but-not-replaced dead link a CI false negative.

## Reproduction

1. Put a known dead URL with an existing Wayback snapshot in a checked Markdown file.
2. Run the Broken Link Checker workflow.
3. Lychee returns a nonzero `exit_code`.
4. `scripts/check_web_archive.py` finds the snapshot and outputs `all_archived=true`.
5. The terminal failure step is skipped, so the workflow is green although the checked Markdown still points to the dead live URL.

The condition can also be reproduced without depending on a live site: feed the helper a fixture `lychee/out.md` containing `[404] <archived-url>`, observe `all_archived=true`, and evaluate the condition above.

## Workaround

Fail on every nonzero Lychee result while retaining the Wayback step for actionable replacement diagnostics:

```yaml
- name: Fail if broken links were found
  if: always() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0
  run: |
    echo "::error::Broken live links were detected."
    exit 1
```

`always()` ensures the explanation runs even if the Wayback API/helper itself fails.

## Suggested code fix

Change the terminal condition as above and update its message to explain that an archive is a suggested replacement, not a reason to accept the still-broken source link. Add a workflow-structure test asserting the failure condition depends only on Lychee's nonzero exit and does not exempt `all_archived=true`.

Found while auditing link-assistant/formal-ai#999 against template revision `bd07d1ce958cbc852a9ec9eae569f2064172b90f`.

cat > "$p/upstream/python-archive.md" <<'EOF'
## Problem

A Wayback API outage is reported as an unavailable snapshot. At \`7a05d051\`, the Python check returns the same result for a request exception and a valid empty \`archived_snapshots\` response. In both cases the CLI advises that it found no snapshot and tells authors to remove or replace the link. The broken link itself should still fail the check.

## Offline reproduction

Run from the template root with Python 3.11 or newer.

\`\`\`bash
PYTHONPATH=scripts python3 - <<'PY'
from unittest.mock import patch
from check_web_archive import check_wayback_machine

url = "https://example.com/deleted"
with patch("check_web_archive.fetch_json", side_effect=TimeoutError("mock outage")):
    outage = check_wayback_machine(url)
with patch("check_web_archive.fetch_json", return_value={"archived_snapshots": {}}):
    missing = check_wayback_machine(url)
print(outage, missing)
assert outage == missing
PY
\`\`\`

## Workaround and code fix

Keep Lychee's verdict and try a manual Wayback lookup after the API recovers before removing a historical reference. Make \`ArchiveResult\` distinguish available, missing, and unknown. Give request failures and invalid responses the unknown verdict and emit a separate notice without asserting that there is no snapshot. Test a snapshot, an empty result, a timeout, and invalid JSON with mocks. Keep the broken-link failure in all four cases.

Found in the audit for link-foundation/box#135. This concerns the recommendation printed by the archive helper. The workflow-level false success described in #54 is a separate issue.
EOF

## Problem

A Wayback API outage is reported as a missing snapshot. At \`e12a25d7\`, \`WebArchive::snapshot\` returns \`null\` after either multiple unavailable responses or successful responses with an empty snapshot collection. \`WebArchive::review\` then puts both in \`missing\`, so the workflow presents the outage as absence of an archive.

## Offline reproduction

Run from the template root.

\`\`\`bash

require 'scripts/src/WebArchive.php';
use LinkFoundation\\Template\\Pipeline\\{Http, WebArchive};

$url = 'https://example.com/deleted';
$lookup = static fn ($status, $body) => (new WebArchive(
    new Http(static fn () => ['status' => $status, 'body' => $body]),
    static fn () => null,
))->review([$url]);
$outage = $lookup(503, 'Service unavailable');
$missing = $lookup(200, '{"archived_snapshots":{}}');

# Issue #125 / pull request #126 evidence

This directory is the reproducible record behind the CI/CD audit requested by
[issue #125](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/issues/125). It covers all
nine runs named by the issue, every job and annotation in those runs, the
available artifacts, the complete CI/CD trees of the four requested reference
templates, the current hive-mind guidance, and the issue/PR discussion state.

## Result

The only false verdict among the nine audited runs is `34455018634`. The disk
measurement completed successfully, generated all 27 component measurements,
and uploaded its artifact, but the wrapped command had deleted the wrapper's
own private files.
That converted command exit 0 into wrapper exit 1 and discarded nearly all
live output. `scripts/ci/run-with-budget-warning.sh` now keeps parent-owned
state under `RUNNER_TEMP`, independently of the child's `TMPDIR`.

The deliberately forced-verbose final gate then exposed a second, latent
defect: raw xtrace printed live credentials in three code paths. Staged
secretlint stopped the affected logs before commit or push. Zizmor now suspends
tracing around token handling, while registry probe and credential preflight
emit state-only diagnostics. The canary regression changed from three secrecy
failures to six total passes, and clean real-token online logs replaced the
quarantined copies.

The other signal is accurate:

- three failure annotations all describe that one propagated failure;
- one link-check notice points to its successful report;
- four Docker Hub copy attempts genuinely failed with HTTP/2
  `PROTOCOL_ERROR`, were visibly retried, and succeeded on attempt two;
- the remaining matches are package-manager warnings, checker summaries,
  fixture assertions, echoed scripts, schema fields, or filenames.

## Runs audited

All nine started at `2026-09-10T08:24:48Z` on merge commit
`90f1e2d95adbb0beb132da366b28d14a3746347c`.

| Run | Workflow | Conclusion | Jobs | Annotations |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `34455018688` | Links | success | 2 | 1 notice |
| `34455018700` | Workflows | success | 3 | 0 |
| `34455018611` | Docs | success | 2 | 0 |
| `34455018674` | File sizes | success | 2 | 0 |
| `34455018599` | Dockerfiles | success | 2 | 0 |
| `34455018650` | Security | success | 5 | 0 |
| `34455018681` | Scripts | success | 8 | 0 |
| `34455018634` | Measure Disk Space and Update README | **failure** | 3 | 3 failures |
| `34455018919` | Build and Release Docker Image | success | 99 | 0 |

`runs/index.json` is the machine-readable version of this table. It was built
from the Actions API rather than inferred from log text.

## Directory map

- `issue.json`, `issue-comments.json`: complete issue and comment payloads.
- `pr*.json`, `related-pr-124*.json`: PR #126 and the merge that triggered the
  audited runs, including all three GitHub review/comment channels.
- `runs/`: run metadata and every job for each run.
- `annotations/`: every check-run annotation, fetched with pagination.
- `ci-logs/`: complete logs for eight runs and the official per-job archive for
  the 99-job release run; see `ci-logs/README.md`.
- `artifacts/`: artifact API listings and every non-expired artifact available
  during collection. `artifacts/index.tsv` maps ids to files.
- `local-tests/`: complete local verification results, including the official
  complete experiment run and the deliberately forced-verbose diagnostic run.
- `analysis/`: requirements, timeline, root causes, alternatives, the complete
  warning/error census, and before/after reproductions.
- `templates/`: full tracked file trees and copies of every CI/CD-relevant file
  from the JavaScript, Python, Rust, and PHP templates.
- `research/`: primary GitHub documentation and related runner reports.
- `upstream/`: duplicate search, submitted report, and returned API record for
  [JavaScript template issue #189](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/189).

## Reproduce the analysis

```bash
bash experiments/issue-125/census-warnings-errors.sh
bash experiments/issue-125/snapshot-templates.sh
bash experiments/issue-125/compare-template-roles.sh \
  > dev/log/issues/125/pulls/126/templates/script-role-matrix.tsv
bash experiments/issue-125/compare-template-roles.sh --workflows \
  > dev/log/issues/125/pulls/126/templates/workflow-role-matrix.tsv
bash experiments/test-issue125-budget-state-survives-tmp-cleanup.sh
bash experiments/test-issue125-verbose-secret-redaction.sh
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Index the saved template trees and Actions annotations for the issue audit."""

import gzip
import io
from pathlib import Path
import re
from zipfile import ZipFile

EVIDENCE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "dev/log/issues/135/pulls/136"
REPOSITORIES = ("box", "js", "rust", "python", "php")
CI_PREFIXES = (".github/", ".githooks/", ".husky/", ".changeset/", "changelog.d/", "scripts/")
ROOT_CONFIGS = {
    ".gitattributes", ".gitignore", ".hadolint.yaml", ".jscpd.json", ".lycheeignore",
    ".nvmrc", ".php-cs-fixer.dist.php", ".pre-commit-config.yaml", ".prettierignore",
    ".prettierrc", ".python-version", ".ruff.toml", ".secretlintrc.json", "Cargo.lock",
    "Cargo.toml", "Dockerfile", "VERSION", "bunfig.toml", "composer.json",
    "composer.lock", "deno.json", "deno.lock", "eslint.config.js", "global.json",
    "lychee.toml", "package-lock.json", "package.json", "phpstan.neon.dist",
    "phpunit.xml.dist", "pyproject.toml", "requirements-dev.in",
    "requirements-dev.txt", "rust-toolchain.toml", "uv.lock",
}


def write_template_index():
    roles = {}
    for repo in REPOSITORIES:
        for name in (EVIDENCE / "github" / f"{repo}.tree").read_text().splitlines():
            if name.startswith(CI_PREFIXES) or name in ROOT_CONFIGS:
                path = Path(name)
                role = path.stem.lower().replace("_", "-")
                if name.startswith(".github/actions/"):
                    role = "/".join(path.parts[2:])
                roles.setdefault((path.parts[0], role), {}).setdefault(repo, []).append(name)

    with (EVIDENCE / "github/ci-role-index.tsv").open("w") as output:
        print("area", "role", *REPOSITORIES, sep="\\t", file=output)
        for (area, role), entries in sorted(roles.items()):
            print(area, role, *(", ".join(entries.get(repo, ())) for repo in REPOSITORIES),
                  sep="\\t", file=output)


def write_log_index():
    marker = re.compile(r"Z (?:##\\[(?:warning|error|notice)\\]|::(?:warning|error|notice)(?=[: ]))")
    with (EVIDENCE / "github/actions-command-census.tsv").open("w") as output:
        print("run", "archive member", "line", "message", sep="\\t", file=output)

        def scan(run, member, lines):
            for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
                if marker.search(line):
                    print(run, member, number, line.strip().replace("\\t", "\\\\t"),
                          sep="\\t", file=output)

        for path in sorted((EVIDENCE / "ci-logs").iterdir()):
            run = path.name.split(".")[0]
            if path.suffix == ".gz":
                with gzip.open(path, "rt", errors="replace") as stream:
                    scan(run, path.name, stream)
            elif path.suffix == ".zip":
                with ZipFile(path) as archive:
                    for member in sorted(archive.namelist()):
                        if re.match(r"^\\d+_.+\\.txt$", member):
                            with io.TextIOWrapper(archive.open(member), errors="replace") as stream:
                                scan(run, member, stream)


write_template_index()
write_log_index()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Index the saved template trees and Actions annotations for the issue audit."""

import gzip
import io
from pathlib import Path
import re
from zipfile import ZipFile

EVIDENCE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "dev/log/issues/135/pulls/136"
REPOSITORIES = ("box", "js", "rust", "python", "php")
CI_PREFIXES = (".github/", ".githooks/", ".husky/", ".changeset/", "changelog.d/", "scripts/")
ROOT_CONFIGS = {
    ".gitattributes", ".gitignore", ".hadolint.yaml", ".jscpd.json", ".lycheeignore",
    ".nvmrc", ".php-cs-fixer.dist.php", ".pre-commit-config.yaml", ".prettierignore",
    ".prettierrc", ".python-version", ".ruff.toml", ".secretlintrc.json", "Cargo.lock",
    "Cargo.toml", "Dockerfile", "VERSION", "bunfig.toml", "composer.json",
    "composer.lock", "deno.json", "deno.lock", "eslint.config.js", "global.json",
    "lychee.toml", "package-lock.json", "package.json", "phpstan.neon.dist",
    "phpunit.xml.dist", "pyproject.toml", "requirements-dev.in",
    "requirements-dev.txt", "rust-toolchain.toml", "uv.lock",
}


def write_template_index():
    roles = {}
    for repo in REPOSITORIES:
        for name in (EVIDENCE / "github" / f"{repo}.tree").read_text().splitlines():
            if name.startswith(CI_PREFIXES) or name in ROOT_CONFIGS:
                path = Path(name)
                role = path.stem.lower().replace("_", "-")
                if name.startswith(".github/actions/"):
                    role = "/".join(path.parts[2:])
                roles.setdefault((path.parts[0], role), {}).setdefault(repo, []).append(name)

    with (EVIDENCE / "github/ci-role-index.tsv").open("w") as output:
        print("area", "role", *REPOSITORIES, sep="\t", file=output)
        for (area, role), entries in sorted(roles.items()):
            print(area, role, *(", ".join(entries.get(repo, ())) for repo in REPOSITORIES),
                  sep="\t", file=output)


def write_log_index():
    marker = re.compile(r"Z (?:##\[(?:warning|error|notice)\]|::(?:warning|error|notice)(?=[: ]))")
    with (EVIDENCE / "github/actions-command-census.tsv").open("w") as output:
        print("run", "archive member", "line", "message", sep="\t", file=output)

        def scan(run, member, lines):
            for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
                if marker.search(line):
                    print(run, member, number, line.strip().replace("\t", "\\t"),
                          sep="\t", file=output)

        for path in sorted((EVIDENCE / "ci-logs").iterdir()):
            run = path.name.split(".")[0]
            if path.suffix == ".gz":
                with gzip.open(path, "rt", errors="replace") as stream:
                    scan(run, path.name, stream)
            elif path.suffix == ".zip":
                with ZipFile(path) as archive:
                    for member in sorted(archive.namelist()):
                        if re.match(r"^\d+_.+\.txt$", member):
                            with io.TextIOWrapper(archive.open(member), errors="replace") as stream:
                                scan(run, member, stream)

# lychee ignore patterns — regex matched against the URL.
#
# Ported from the reference template (issue #115, R5) and extended with the

# Localhost and local development URLs
http://localhost
https://localhost
http://127\.0\.0\.1
https://127\.0\.0\.1

# Example/placeholder URLs commonly used in documentation
https://example\.com
http://example\.com

# npmjs.com returns 403 to link checkers (bot protection)
https://www\.npmjs\.com

# medium.com returns 403 to link checkers (bot protection)
https://medium\.com

# web.archive.org returns 502 to link checkers (bot protection)
https://web\.archive\.org

# GitHub repository settings pages require admin authentication; an anonymous
# GET is 404 by design, for a URL the maintainer needs and that is correct.
https://github\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/settings/

# Docker Hub account settings redirect to the login flow, which lychee follows
# in a loop and rejects. Same reason as the GitHub settings pages above.
https://hub\.docker\.com/settings/

# manpages.ubuntu.com answers 503 under any load, and gnu.org rate-limits

https://manpages\.ubuntu\.com
https://www\.gnu\.org

# packages.ubuntu.com takes 19-30s to answer, so lychee's 30s timeout trips on
# it often enough to fail the scheduled run on main. The pages are correct.
https://packages\.ubuntu\.com

https://(arm\.)?flatassembler\.net

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run a checkout's link recovery against a localhost HEAD/GET disagreement."""

import argparse
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile
from threading import Thread


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_HEAD(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()

    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(404)
        self.end_headers()

    def log_message(self, *_args):
        pass


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("checkout", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("command", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler) as server, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as work:
        thread = Thread(target=server.serve_forever)
        thread.start()
        try:
            root = Path(work)
            url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/missing"
            report = root / "report.md"
            report.write_text(
                "# Summary\n| Errors | 1 |\n| Timeouts | 0 |\n"
                "## Errors per input\n"
                f"* [503] <{url}> | Rejected status code: 503\n"
            )
            outputs = root / "output.txt"
            outputs.touch()
            env = dict(
                os.environ,
                LYCHEE_OUTPUT=str(report),
                RECOVERED_OUTPUT=str(root / "recovered.txt"),
                GITHUB_OUTPUT=str(outputs),
                LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE="2",
                RECHECK_BUDGET_SECONDS="1",
                RECHECK_WAIT_MS="20",
            )
            subprocess.run(args.command, cwd=args.checkout, env=env, check=True, timeout=5)
            if "all_recovered=true" in outputs.read_text():
                print("FAIL: HEAD 200 concealed GET 404")
                return 1
            print("PASS: GET…ved")
            return 0
        finally:
            server.shutdown()
            thread.join()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Static checks over the shell scripts that build and measure the boxes.
#
# Why this workflow exists (issue #115): the two scripts that generate a second
# script from a quoted heredoc both referenced parent-shell variables that the
# generated script could never see. One of them broke `Measure Disk Space and
# Update README` on main (run 33972074753); the other, scripts/ubuntu-24-server-install.sh,
# had the identical defect and no job that would ever have run it. Checks that
# only ever run on a developer's laptop are not checks, so they run here.
#
# The filters below are the union of what every gate in this file reads, not a
# guess at it: the shell for shellcheck, shfmt and the heredoc scan; .githooks/
# because git requires an extensionless `pre-commit`, which no `*.sh` glob ever
# sees; the JavaScript for the syntax gate; and .mjs, .js, .py, .yml and .yaml
# for the awk scan, which reads every language that can embed an awk program.
# `scripts/ci/check-workflow-path-coverage.mjs` derives that requirement from
# these lines and fails when a gate here reads a file none of them can match -
# which is what the mjs-syntax job did for its entire first day (issue #121).

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '**.sh'
      - '**.bash'
      - '**.mjs'
      - '**.js'
      - '**.py'
      - '**.yml'
      - '**.yaml'
      - '.githooks/**'
      - '.github/workflows/**'
      - 'ubuntu/**'
      - 'tests/**'

    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run-experiments.sh - Run the repository's experiment/regression suites.
#
# Usage:
#   bash scripts/ci/run-experiments.sh [--list] [--list-inputs] [--verbose]
#
# Why this exists (issue #115, RC-9). The repository had 27 suites under
# experiments/ and the workflows referenced 5 of them. The other 22 ran only
# when a developer remembered to run them by hand — which is to say, they were
# not checks. Two of them (test-issue90, test-issue92) had been *crashing* on
# any machine without a UTF-8 locale, and nothing noticed, because nothing ran
# them.
#
# So this discovers suites rather than listing them: a new experiments/*.sh is
# picked up automatically, and the only way to not run one is to name it in
# SKIP_SUITES below, with a reason.
#
# Environment:
#   SUITE_TIMEOUT   per-suite timeout in seconds, default 300
#   BOX_VERBOSE     set to 1 to echo each suite's full output, default off
#                   (failing suites always have their output printed)

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." || exit 1

SUITE_TIMEOUT="${SUITE_TIMEOUT:-300}"
BOX_VERBOSE="${BOX_VERBOSE:-0}"
LIST_ONLY=0
LIST_INPUTS=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --list)
      LIST_ONLY=1
      shift
      ;;
    --list-inputs)
      LIST_INPUTS=1
      shift
      ;;
    -v | --verbose)
      BOX_VERBOSE=1
      shift
      ;;
    -h | --help)
      sed -n '2,22p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \?//'
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      echo "run-experiments.sh: unknown option $1" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# Suites excluded from the default run, each with the reason. Keep this list
# short and justified; "it is slow" is not a reason to stop running a check.
#
# The keys are quoted, and that is not a style choice. An unquoted subscript is
# an arithmetic expression to any tool that parses one, and shfmt formats it as
# such: `[node-lts-integration-test.sh]` came back from the formatter as
# `[node - lts - integration - test.sh]`. Bash does not evaluate subscripts of
# an associative array, so the key silently became a different string, all
# three entries stopped matching, and a run that should have skipped three
# suites ran them and reported two failures instead. Nothing complained. The
# assertion below is what turns that back into an error.
declare -A SKIP_SUITES=(
  ['node-lts-integration-test.sh']="needs network: resolves the live Node LTS feed (covered by the version-policy CI tier)"
  ['rust-refresh-layer-test.sh']="needs docker: builds layers to measure image size"
  ['verify-full-box-tooling.sh']="needs docker and a pulled full-box image (tens of GB); manual probe behind scripts/ci/test-box.sh"
  ['test-issue121-provenance-metadata-leak.sh']="needs docker: drives a real buildx build to reproduce the metadata provenance leak (its offline twin, test-issue121-log-injection.sh, runs here)"
  ['measure-issue121-apt-recommends.sh']="needs docker and a network: resolves apt dependency plans in ubuntu:24.04 to measure what --no-install-recommends drops; a measurement, not an assertion (its recorded output is in dev/log/issues/121/pulls/122/apt-recommends/)"
  ['reproduce-issue123-zizmor-offline-audits.sh']="needs docker, a network and a GitHub token: run…re)"
  ['reproduce-issue133-containerd-pid.sh']="needs docker and a privileged box-dind image: commits a running nested daemon and resumes it to reproduce the stale containerd pid file (its offline twin, test-issue133-stale-pid-files.sh, runs here; tests/dind/example-snapshot-resume.sh covers it in PR CI)"
  ['reproduce-issue121-actionlint-version-gap.sh']="needs docker and a network: runs two pinned actionlint images over the same fixtures to measure which checks the older one cannot make; a measurement, not an assertion (the version floor it argues for is asserted offline by test-issue121-workflow-audit-scope.sh)"
)

# Where the skip names come from, which is the repository's suite directory
# even when EXPERIMENTS_DIR points somewhere else for this runner's own tests.
SKIP_ROOT="experiments"

# A skip entry that names nothing is indistinguishable from no entry at all:
# the suite runs, and whoever wrote the exclusion never learns it stopped
# applying. Renaming a suite and forgetting the list has the same shape as the
# formatter defect above, so both are caught here.
for skipped_name in "${!SKIP_SUITES[@]}"; do
  if [ ! -f "$SKIP_ROOT/$skipped_name" ]; then
    echo "::error title=run-experiments::SKIP_SUITES names '$skipped_name', which does not exist under $SKIP_ROOT/. Either the suite was renamed or the subscript was rewritten; an entry that matches nothing silently stops skipping." >&2
    exit 2
  fi
done

# Overridable so this runner's own regression suite can drive it against
# fixtures. The thing that runs every other check had no check of its own.
EXPERIMENTS_DIR="${EXPERIMENTS_DIR:-experiments}"
BEST-PRACTICES-VERIFICATION.md
LOG-DISPOSITIONS.md
PRIOR-ART.md
REQUIREMENTS.md
ROOT-CAUSES.md
SOLUTIONS.md

cat > "$p/README.md" <<'EOF'
# CI/CD audit for issue 135 and PR 136

The audit covers the nine runs named in [issue 135](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/issues/135), their job and artifact metadata, the surrounding default-branch history, the [PR discussion](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/pull/136), and all four requested reference trees. The initial issue comments, PR conversation, inline reviews, submitted reviews, and required sub-issues were empty. The snapshots and inventories are in [github](github/).

## Requirements and verification

| Requirement | Finding and implementation | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Restore Links on main | The GitHub project formerly cited in the issue 80 case study returned 404 in two consecutive weekly scans. The case study now links to the specific Wayback snapshot identified by both runs. | Run 45443984715 lines 304, 336, 355 and 395, run 44115877567, and the GitHub API 404 in [verification](verification/). The archive replay from the local network was rate-limited. The snapshot URL came from the two independent Actions lookups. |
| Fix false link verdicts across the pipeline | Retry completed, fully accounted-for scans only. Restrict rechecks to transient failures. Match the scanner's GET method and accepted statuses, preserve final failures for an otherwise recoverable URL, and leave anchor and local file validation to the scanner. Distinguish a failed scanner from a scan with broken links. | \`test-issue135-link-verdicts.sh\`, \`test-issue121-links-recheck.sh\`, and \`test-issue131-links-recheck.sh\`. The bounded localhost experiment gives HEAD 200 and GET 404: Box's baseline passes falsely and the fixed Box rejects recovery. |
| Make archive diagnostics truthful | Both helpers parse the report's Errors and Timeouts sections; ignore successful redirects and the runner footer and preserve exact URL punctuation. Separate a valid response with no snapshot from a timeout, error status, or malformed payload. Bound requests and retain the original link verdict. | \`test-issue135-link-verdicts.sh\`, including mocked absent, present, unreachable, and malformed archive responses. The Links job also runs tests that enforce the terminal gate. |
| Restore disk measurement | The historical temporary-file bug had already been repaired on main. Add its regression to measurement preflight. Require preflight success before installation, require fresh output, validate it before replacing tracked data and rendering README, and only publish from main. Distinguish git diff errors from a changed file. | \`test-issue125-budget-state-survives-tmp-cleanup.sh\` and \`test-issue135-measure-workflow.sh\`. [Manual branch validation](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/actions/runs/45954663314) executes the installer and output pipeline without publication. |
| Audit remaining workflows, warnings, errors and misleading passes | Inspect the six other named workflow groups and the successful and failing adjacent runs. Retain the security, formatting, file size, docs, Dockerfile, workflow and release gates. Fix the Scripts fixture that could fail on a valid anchor. | [Run and signal disposition](#run-and-signal-disposition), [extracted annotations](github/actions-command-census.tsv), and the PR workflow runs. |
| Compare all four template trees and adopt applicable practices | Pin all trees, index every workflow, action and CI script, compare their roles and root tools, and map Hive Mind's practices to the Box pipeline. | [Template comparison](templates.md), complete tracked trees and CI file fingerprints in [github](github/). |
| Report genuinely shared issues | Reproduced wrong HTTP-method recovery in JS, Python and PHP. Reproduced unavailable/missing archive conflation in Python and PHP. Rust's current check already uses GET. | Five [public reports](upstream/reports.txt) with isolated reproduction, workaround, and code suggestions. [Fixture output](verification/). |
| Leave diagnostics available for the next run | The Links dispatch input enables scanner verbosity and per-request retry diagnostics. Measurement dispatch exposes the existing opt-in diagnostics to the budget wrapper. | Workflow regression assertions. Both dispatch inputs default to false. |
| Ship one reviewed change with release automation | Use the repository's changeset to trigger an automatic patch after merge. Keep the evidence and regressions in PR 136. | [Changeset](../../../../../../.changeset/ci-verdicts.md), Actions checks for the current PR head, and Git ancestry of main. |

## Timeline and root causes

| UTC date | Evidence and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-09-10 | Measurement run [34455018634](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/actions/runs/34455018634) failed. Lines 649–655 show removal of the wrapper's state after the installer cleans system temp, while 2453–2454 show the propagated exit 1. The installer deliberately removes files inside system temp; the parent wrapper had stored its status and forwarding files there. PR 126 moved state into \`RUNNER_TEMP\`. The historical artifact had expired by audit time; our earlier [PR 126 evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/tree/main/dev/log/issues/125/pulls/126) preserves the successful measurements. |
| 2026-10-06 | Links [37466341052](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/actions/runs/37466341052) failed on an HTTP 503 from a healthy GitHub Discussion. This was a temporary response. Commit \`2095b5c\` added bounded recovery of temporary status codes. |
| 2026-10-11 | Scripts [38157957100](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/actions/runs/38157957100) failed the valid-anchor fixture at lines 1070–1102. The fixture piped complete program output through \`grep -q\` with \`pipefail\`. A match lets grep exit before the producer finishes, so the producer can receive SIGPIPE. The committed test now captures output and command status separately before checking the anchor. |
| 2026-10-13 | Links [38406835991](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/actions/runs/38406835991) identified 30-second timeouts for the Ubuntu package page. Existing commit \`d8d7c0c\` documents that service in the ignore file. |
| 2026-10-14 | The release, docs, sizes, scripts, workflows and links runs for \`a63b605\` succeeded. |
| 2026-11-10 | Links [42833999978](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/actions/runs/42833999978) was green on the same source subsequently checked by the November failures. This bounds the observation window without establishing when the upstream GitHub repository stopped being public. |
| 2026-11-17 / 2026-11-24 | Both scheduled Links scans reached the old repository URL and returned 404. Both suggested the archive from 2020-10-11. The repeatable live 404 explains the failed gate. Local fixture tests separately found the latent false-green and diagnostic defects. |
| 2026-11-27 | Issue 135 was opened and PR 136 linked. The audit reproduced the historical disk regression and link false green, compared the pinned trees, and filed shared defects upstream. |

## Run and signal disposition

| Named run | Recorded result | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 45443984715 Links | Failed | Genuine persistent GitHub 404. Correct the authored link. |
| 45220072505 Security | Passed | CodeQL and secret scanning succeeded. The selected tables and job metadata carry the actual check conclusions. |
| 38633908376 File sizes | Passed | Size gate and its final status passed. |
| 38633908390 Build and Release | Passed | Build and publication completed. The raw GH archive replaces the formatted CLI output, which hit the job-log download request limit. |
| 38633908272 Docs | Passed | Required documentation and final status passed. |
| 38633908325 Scripts | Passed | Static and regression jobs passed. Adjacent earlier anchor failure repaired by this PR. |
| 38633908273 Workflows | Passed | Workflow lint/audit and terminal status passed. |
| 34455018599 Dockerfiles | Passed | Hadolint accepted the Dockerfiles and final status passed. |
| 34455018634 Measure Disk Space | Failed | False negative for the installer, accurate failure for evidence capture. Existing wrapper repair plus new preflight, freshness and publication checks. |

The GitHub command census indexes both streamed logs and raw job archives with line numbers. Repeated terminal errors report the same failed dependency. Successful scan notices point to reports; retries identify recovered URLs. Release job traces also contain commands that would emit warnings in other scenarios. A warning string in a step's echoed shell body is not a runner warning. Actual warnings from stripped manpages are expected in the minimal image, and temporary registry retries can succeed without dropping the final publication verification. Prior suppressed-host cases, prototype fixtures and unexplained external failures were kept distinct. Historical CI statuses show that a green build alone could miss the wrapper ordering, report completeness and GET/HEAD defects.

## Design alternatives and prior art

- Changing the case-study reference preserves source attribution and the historical example. Removing it loses detail, and broadly accepting 404 would hide other dead links. The existing Wayback host exemption addresses bot/rate protection. Preserve the timestamped target given by the runner.
- Lychee remains the scanner and the authority for anchors. Its [CLI](https://lychee.cli.rs/guides/cli/) uses GET by default. [Lychee issue 2297](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/issues/2297) already tracks connect-phase retries; the bounded retry helper works around that gap. Switching to structured JSON could simplify report validation in a future action change. Pinning the existing textual contract keeps the PR's human-readable job summary and both consumers together. PHP and Python's archives illustrate why a single boolean or nullable URL cannot describe lookup availability.
- GitHub's [job dependency semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/using-jobs-in-a-workflow) already give the needed preflight gate. A fresh output pathname allows the existing validator and renderer to run as-is under their normal entry points. Timestamp heuristics and the committed JSON cannot prove the installer produced a document. The budget wrapper and existing status gate preserve capacity and outcome diagnostics.
- The existing Box Actions and shell tooling already solve image-specific CI. Replacing the release chain with package workflows would lose native multi-architecture builds and registry validation. Compare interfaces and failure semantics using the role matrix, then reuse matching practices.

## Evidence and reproduction

- [ci-logs](ci-logs/) holds compressed Actions logs. For \`.log.gz\`, use \`gzip -dc\`; for \`.zip\`, use \`unzip -l\` and \`unzip -p ARCHIVE 'MEMBER'\`. The adjacent \`.error.txt\` files document the formatted CLI's download-limit failures before the raw archive fallback.
- [artifact-metadata](artifact-metadata/) and [job-metadata](job-metadata/) preserve GitHub API details for the cited runs. The older artifact expired.
- [github](github/) holds the primary data and the complete tree inventories. [research](research/) contains the pinned Lychee formatter and the prior workflow. [upstream](upstream/) contains submitted text and issue URLs.
- From the repository root, run \`python3 experiments/issue-135/index-evidence.py\` to regenerate the census and role index. Run \`python3 experiments/issue-135/reproduce-head-get.py . node scripts/ci/recheck-broken-links.mjs\` for the bounded network-free loopback reproduction.
- Run the new offline suites with \`bash experiments/test-issue135-link-verdicts.sh\` and \`bash experiments/test-issue135-measure-workflow.sh\`. Each uses mocks or validates narrowly scoped workflow structure. The runner installs the real components in the manual measurement. 
EOF
sed -i 's/[[:blank:]]*$//' "$p/README.md"`
}))

| --- | --- |

| Workflow audit, path filtering, terminal status, superseded runs and job budgets | Box uses workflow syntax/lint, Zizmor, checkout-credential checks, path coverage, and per-job budget checks, together with a final aggregate check. JS and Rust additionally auto-rerun selected infrastructure failures. Box classifies failures in its native release, registry, and supersede helpers. A blanket rerun can delay stable failures and duplicate expensive builds. |
| Tests, examples, language gates and app builds | JS first-gate/example and Rust desktop workflows check the package template's application and architecture contracts. Package-specific source, lockfile and runtime matrices target delivered package code. Box provisions several toolchains but has no product package manifest for those managers. |
| Release plumbing, credentials, state and artifact transport | Templates publish packages and some examples or desktop binaries. Box publishes native AMD64/Arm64 images and consumes digest/manifest, registry credential probes and build-chain artifacts. Changesets drive versions, the actual merge is checked, and per-registry retry helpers classify failures. Retain workflow-specific publication logic and only use archive transport for a demonstrated artifact service problem. |

Language package install and audit policies apply to template package lockfiles. Box's dependency surface consists primarily of the base image, tools installed by Dockerfiles, and external actions. Keep its dedicated workflow, and use ordinary job prerequisites and validated artifacts to eliminate false results. |

## Hive Mind practices

The source guidance is [the Hive Mind CI/CD document](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md). This table records the Box checks and the specific application choices that affect verdicts.

| Practice | Application in Box |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Run relevant checks | Workflow path filters cover lint inputs, tested by \`check-workflow-path-coverage.mjs\`. Release's path classifier determines the affected image tiers. PR validation runs fast tests even when expensive publication is disabled, and a manual or main run can exercise the installer. |
| 2. File line limits | \`file-sizes.yml\` invokes \`check-file-line-limits.sh\` and propagates failures. |
| 3. Automated formatting | Scripts and local hooks use \`run-shfmt.sh\` for shipped and test shell. |
| 4. Static analysis | Scripts check heredocs, awk portability, JavaScript and Python syntax, and ShellCheck. Dockerfiles use Hadolint. Security uses CodeQL where supported. |
| 5. Fast failures | Release validates inputs before image build jobs. The disk install now requires its fast preflight, including a wrapper cleanup regression. |
| 6. Changesets | \`.changeset/ci-verdicts.md\` triggers an automated patch. Changeset scripts validate, coalesce and apply changes before publication. |
| 7. Check the merge result | \`simulate-fresh-merge\` runs relevant PR workflows against a fresh merge; use repository-controlled safe checkout behavior. |
| 8. Local hooks | \`.githooks/pre-commit\` and \`scripts/install-git-hooks.sh\` expose the same checks early. |
| 9. Automated releases | The release orchestrator prepares versions, calls native build workflows, creates multi-arch manifests and validates publication. |
| 10. Concurrency | Scoped concurrency groups and the supersede helper ensure replaced runs can stop without converting current failures into successes. Measure's slow request and PR validation use separate groups. |
| 11. Detect secrets | Security uses Secretlint and the Box experiment suite tests masking opt-in credential diagnostics. Existing checkout permission validation remains in place. |
| 12. Documentation | Dedicated Docs and Links workflows. Link recovery leaves anchors/local files to Lychee and keeps 404 and archived-only live failures red. |
| 13. Native container architectures | Release tiers use Ubuntu AMD64 and Arm64 runners, publishing combined platform manifests. |
| 14. Lint workflows | Workflow syntax, Zizmor and explicit job/status/path and permission checks validate workflow behavior. |
| 15. Audit dependency trees | Existing workflow dependency audits check actions; Box's image dependencies are installed by the platform/Dockerfiles, and the PR version and runtime scenarios verify those contracts. Template-specific npm/Cargo/uv/Composer lockfile audits require a package dependency tree. |
| 16. Preflight publishing | \`preflight\` verifies release credentials and relevant registry operations. PR jobs do not require write credentials; disk measurements run on the branch but can only publish from main. |
| 17. Classify the real failure | Link scan failure differs from unavailability of the scanner or archive service. Disk generation validates fresh files before output publishing. Existing terminal status, supersede and retry classifiers preserve cancellations and originating failure types. |
EOF

find "$p/job-metadata" -type f -size 0 -print
cat "$p/verification/wayback-availability.log"
git diff --check

491-**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. 498-- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.

v26.13.1
#!/usr/bin/env node

/**
 * Fails when a checkout does not say what happens to the job's token.
 *
 * `actions/checkout` authenticates by writing an AUTHORIZATION header into the
 * repository's git configuration, and by default it leaves it there: every
 * later step in that job can read it back and push with it. Setting
 * `persist-credentials: false` makes checkout take it out again at the end of
 * its own step, which is visible in a job log as `Removing HTTP extra header`
 * before the first real step instead of during `Post job cleanup`.
 *
 * Thirty of this repository's fifty-five checkouts said nothing, so thirty
 * jobs kept it — including `js / build-js-amd64`, which held it for 427
 * seconds while a docker build ran with the workspace as its build context,
 * and `Measure Component Disk Space`, which held it for 886
 * (experiments/reproduce-issue121-checkout-credentials.sh measures both out of
 * the downloaded run logs). zizmor has the audit for exactly this —
 * `artipacked` — and reports it at severity Low, which is under the floor the
 * workflow gate runs at, so it was filtered out thirty times: a check that
 * could not fail, which is what issue #121 is about.
 *
 * The rule here is not "always drop it". It is that the setting must be a
 * decision, and the decision must match what the job does:
 *
 *   - a job that writes to the remote must keep the credential;
 *   - every other job must drop it;
 *   - saying nothing is neither, and is reported as such, because the default
 *     is the unsafe one and silence hides which of the two was meant.
 *
 * "Writes to the remote" is derived, not listed: the job's `run:` lines are
 * followed into the scripts they call, transitively, and a `git push` anywhere
 * in that closure makes the job a writer. So a job that starts pushing through
 * a new helper is classified correctly without anyone remembering to update a
 * list here.
 *
 * Reads are anonymous under `persist-credentials: false` and that is fine
 * because this repository is public; the same reasoning, and the same caveat,
 * is written out at the fetch in scripts/ci/simulate-fresh-merge.sh.
 *

#!/usr/bin/env node

/**
 * Fails when a checkout does not say what happens to the job's token.
 *
 * `actions/checkout` authenticates by writing an AUTHORIZATION header into the
 * repository's git configuration, and by default it leaves it there: every
 * later step in that job can read it back and push with it. Setting
 * `persist-credentials: false` makes checkout take it out again at the end of
 * its own step, which is visible in a job log as `Removing HTTP extra header`
 * before the first real step instead of during `Post job cleanup`.
 *
 * Thirty of this repository's fifty-five checkouts said nothing, so thirty
 * jobs kept it — including `js / build-js-amd64`, which held it for 427
 * seconds while a docker build ran with the workspace as its build context,
 * and `Measure Component Disk Space`, which held it for 886
 * (experiments/reproduce-issue121-checkout-credentials.sh measures both out of
 * the downloaded run logs). zizmor has the audit for exactly this —
 * `artipacked` — and reports it at severity Low, which is under the floor the
 * workflow gate runs at, so it was filtered out thirty times: a check that
 * could not fail, which is what issue #121 is about.
 *
 * The rule here is not "always drop it". It is that the setting must be a
 * decision, and the decision must match what the job does:
 *
 *   - a job that writes to the remote must keep the credential;
 *   - every other job must drop it;
 *   - saying nothing is neither, and is reported as such, because the default
 *     is the unsafe one and silence hides which of the two was meant.
 *
 * "Writes to the remote" is derived, not listed: the job's `run:` lines are
 * followed into the scripts they call, transitively, and a `git push` anywhere
 * in that closure makes the job a writer. So a job that starts pushing through
 * a new helper is classified correctly without anyone remembering to update a
 * list here.
 *
 * Reads are anonymous under `persist-credentials: false` and that is fine
 * because this repository is public; the same reasoning, and the same caveat,
 * is written out at the fetch in scripts/ci/simulate-fresh-merge.sh.
 *

Fixes #135

## Findings and changes

- The November scheduled link failures both came from a persistent GitHub 404 in the issue 80 case study. The reference now points to the timestamped Wayback snapshot confirmed by the availability API.
- Link recovery now matches Lychee's GET, requires complete failure reports, and preserves permanent, local and anchor failures. A scanner execution error and an unavailable Wayback lookup each get their own diagnostic.
- The historical disk failure came from installer cleanup deleting the observer's temporary files. The existing fix now has a regression in measurement preflight. The main measurement depends on that preflight, validates a fresh JSON file before updating tracked files, and only publishes from main.
- The Scripts anchor fixture now captures the producer's output before checking it, removing a SIGPIPE race. A changeset triggers the automatic patch release.

## Reproduction and verification

- Run \`python3 experiments/issue-135/reproduce-head-get.py . node scripts/ci/recheck-broken-links.mjs\`. The loopback endpoint answers HEAD 200 and GET 404. The old helper reports recovery and the new helper keeps the failure.

name: Dockerfiles

# Static checks over the Dockerfiles that define the boxes.
#
# Why this workflow exists (issue #115): this repository *is* a collection of
# Dockerfiles, and no linter had ever read one. actionlint reads the workflows,
# scripts.yml reads every *.sh, and the 23 Dockerfiles were the one body of
# source with no check at all. `apt install` instead of `apt-get install` was
# sitting in ubuntu/24.04/js/Dockerfile and in nine install scripts, printing
# "WARNING: apt does not have a stable CLI interface" into every box build -
# a warning nobody was looking for, because nothing collected it.

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      # A GitHub filter pattern is matched against the whole path from the
      # repository root, and `**/` requires a directory, so '**/Dockerfile'
      # does not match the root Dockerfile - the one this repository's own
      # image is built from (issue #121).
      - 'Dockerfile'
      - '**/Dockerfile'
      - '**/Dockerfile.*'
      - '**/*.Dockerfile'
      - '.hadolint.yaml'
      - 'scripts/ci/run-hadolint.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/dockerfiles.yml'
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      # A GitHub filter pattern is matched against the whole path from the
      # repository root, and `**/` requires a directory, so '**/Dockerfile'
      # does not match the root Dockerfile - the one this repository's own
      # image is built from (issue #121).
      - 'Dockerfile'
      - '**/Dockerfile'
      - '**/Dockerfile.*'
      - '**/*.Dockerfile'
      - '.hadolint.yaml'
      - 'scripts/ci/run-hadolint.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/dockerfiles.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least-privilege default; this job only reads the checked-out tree.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # actions/checkout's first act is `git init`, and a git with no configured
  # `init.defaultBranch` answers it with a thirteen-line advice block - "Using
  # 'master' as the name for the initial branch... this default branch name will
  # change" - at the top of every job log. 19 checkouts in the runs issue #121
  # lists printed 247 lines of it, in jobs where nothing was wrong. No step can
  # fix it, because it is printed before the first step of ours runs; git reads
  # configuration from the environment too, and the environment is there from
  # the start. Ported from the js template, which carries the same three lines
  # with the same reasoning.
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  hadolint:
    name: dockerfiles / hadolint
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Typical run: a few seconds once the image is pulled. The limit is here so
    # a hung docker pull cannot hold a runner for six hours.

# Create measurement script for box user
cat >/tmp/box-measure.sh <<'EOF_BOX'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

JSON_OUTPUT_FILE="${1:-/tmp/disk-space-measurements.json}"

# This script is written from a QUOTED heredoc (<< 'EOF_BOX'), so nothing below
# was expanded when the file was created, and it runs under `su - box` /
# `sudo -i -u box` — a login shell that starts from a clean environment. Every
# version the parent resolved therefore has to be handed in explicitly at the
# call site. Assert them here so an omission fails by name instead of as
# "line 128: NODE_MAJOR: unbound variable", which is how run 33972074753 failed
# on main (issue #115).
: "${NODE_MAJOR:?must be passed in by scripts/measure-disk-space.sh}"
: "${NVM_INSTALL_VERSION:?must be passed in by scripts/measure-disk-space.sh}"
: "${JAVA_MAJOR:?must be passed in by scripts/measure-disk-space.sh}"

BOX_VERBOSE="${BOX_VERBOSE:-0}"
# Trace every command when asked. Off by default: this log is already ~1800
# lines, and `set -x` over a 40-minute install run is unreadable unless you are
# specifically chasing something (issue #115).
[ "$BOX_VERBOSE" = "1" ] && set -x || true

# Logging
log_info() { echo -e "\033[0;34m[*]\033[0m $1"; }
log_debug() { [ "$BOX_VERBOSE" = "1" ] && echo -e "\033[0;36m[debug]\033[0m $1" || true; }
log_success() { echo -e "\033[0;32m[✓]\033[0m $1"; }
log_warning() { echo -e "\033[1;33m[!]\033[0m $1"; }

command_exists() { command -v "$1" &>/dev/null; }

maybe_sudo() {
  if [ "$EUID" -eq 0 ]; then "$@"
  elif command_exists sudo; then sudo "$@"
  eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -x "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" ]]; then
  eval "$("$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" shellenv)"
fi

# --- PHP ---
install_php() {
  if command -v brew &>/dev/null; then
    brew tap shivammathur/php || true
    export HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1
    export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1
    brew install php || true
    # `brew link` prints its "Warning:" lines on a *successful* link, so the
    # output was filtered - but `| grep -v "Warning" || true` made grep's status
    # the pipeline's and then discarded it, so a link that failed was
    # indistinguishable from one that worked. The filter belongs on the output;
    # the status belongs to brew. Anchoring the pattern also stops a line that
    # merely mentions a warning from being deleted with them. (issue #123)
    local brew_link_out="" brew_link_status=0
    brew_link_out="$(brew link --overwrite --force php 2>&1)" || brew_link_status=$?
    if [ "$brew_link_status" -eq 0 ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$brew_link_out" | grep -v '^Warning' || true
    else
      printf '%s\n' "$brew_link_out"
      log_warning "brew link --overwrite --force php failed (exit $brew_link_status)"
    fi
  fi
}
measure_install "PHP (via Homebrew)" "Runtime" install_php

# --- Perlbrew + Perl ---
install_perlbrew_perl() {
  export PERLBREW_ROOT="$HOME/.perl5"
  curl -L https://install.perlbrew.pl | bash

  if [ -f "$PERLBREW_ROOT/etc/bashrc" ]; then
    sed -i 's/\$1/${1:-}/g' "$PERLBREW_ROOT/etc/bashrc" 2>/dev/null || true
    sed -i 's/\$PERLBREW_LIB/${PERLBREW_LIB:-}/g' "$PERLBREW_ROOT/etc/bashrc" 2>/dev/null || true
    sed -i 's/\$outsep/${outsep:-}/g' "$PERLBREW_ROOT/etc/bashrc" 2>/dev/null || true

    set +u
    source "$PERLBREW_ROOT/etc/bashrc"
    set -u

    LATEST_PERL=$(perlbrew available 2>&1 | grep -oE 'perl-5\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)
    if [ -n "$LATEST_PERL" ]; then
      perlbrew install "$LATEST_PERL" --notest || true
      perlbrew switch "$LATEST_PERL" || true
    fi
  fi
}
measure_install "Perlbrew + Perl (latest)" "Runtime" install_perlbrew_perl

measure_install "Swift 6.x" "Runtime" install_swift

log_success "Box user measurements complete"
EOF_BOX

chmod +x /tmp/box-measure.sh

# Resolve JSON output path to absolute before passing to box user.
# 'su - box' and 'sudo -i -u box' both create login shells that change
# the working directory to the box user's home (/home/box). Relative
# paths like 'data/disk-space-measurements.json' would then resolve to the wrong
# location, causing "No such file or directory" errors.
# See docs/case-studies/issue-46 for the full root cause analysis.
JSON_OUTPUT_FILE_ABS="$(realpath "$JSON_OUTPUT_FILE")"
# The box user needs to read and write the JSON file, but the GitHub Actions
# workspace directories (e.g. /home/runner/work/box/box/) are owned by
# 'runner' and typically have mode 750, so 'box' (not in the 'runner' group)
# cannot traverse them even if the file itself is world-readable.
# Solution: copy the JSON file to /tmp (world-accessible, mode 1777), run the
# box measurements against that copy, then copy the result back.
JSON_TMP_COPY="$(mktemp /tmp/disk-space-measurements-XXXXXX.json)"
cp "$JSON_OUTPUT_FILE_ABS" "$JSON_TMP_COPY"
chmod o+rw "$JSON_TMP_COPY"

log_debug "Handing to the box user: NODE_MAJOR=$NODE_MAJOR NVM_INSTALL_VERSION=$NVM_INSTALL_VERSION JAVA_MAJOR=$JAVA_MAJOR BOX_VERBOSE=$BOX_VERBOSE"
log_debug "Generated script: /tmp/box-measure.sh ($(wc -l </tmp/box-measure.sh) lines), JSON copy: $JSON_TMP_COPY"

# Execute box user measurements against the /tmp copy.
# `su -` and `sudo -i` both start a login shell with a fresh environment, so the
# versions resolved above are passed explicitly; /tmp/box-measure.sh asserts
# each one (issue #115). `env` is used rather than a bare VAR=value prefix
# because sudo's env_reset policy rejects unlisted variables.
if [ "$EUID" -eq 0 ]; then
  su - box -c "env NODE_MAJOR='$NODE_MAJOR' NVM_INSTALL_VERSION='$NVM_INSTALL_VERSION' JAVA_MAJOR='$JAVA_MAJOR' BOX_VERBOSE='$BOX_VERBOSE' bash /tmp/box-measure.sh '$JSON_TMP_COPY'"
else
  sudo -i -u box env "NODE_MAJOR=$NODE_MAJOR" "NVM_INSTALL_VERSION=$NVM_INSTALL_VERSION" "JAVA_MAJOR=$JAVA_MAJOR" "BOX_VERBOSE=$BOX_VERBOSE" bash /tmp/box-measure.sh "$JSON_TMP_COPY"
fi

# Copy the updated measurements back to the original location
cp "$JSON_TMP_COPY" "$JSON_OUTPUT_FILE_ABS"
rm -f "$JSON_TMP_COPY"

rm -f /tmp/box-measure.sh

# ============================================================================
# FINALIZE
# ============================================================================
log_step "Finalizing Measurements"

cleanup_for_measurement
FINAL_MB=$(get_disk_usage_mb)
TOTAL_MB=$(awk "BEGIN {printf \"%.2f\", $FINAL_MB - $BASELINE_MB}")

finalize_json_output "$TOTAL_MB"

log_step "Measurement Complete!"
log_success "Total installation size: ${TOTAL_MB}MB"
log_success "Results saved to: $JSON_OUTPUT_FILE"

JSON_OUTPUT_FILE="${1:-/tmp/disk-space-measurements.json}"

# This script is written from a QUOTED heredoc (<< 'EOF_BOX'), so nothing below
# was expanded when the file was created, and it runs under `su - box` /
# `sudo -i -u box` — a login shell that starts from a clean environment. Every
# version the parent resolved therefore has to be handed in explicitly at the
# call site. Assert them here so an omission fails by name instead of as
# "line 128: NODE_MAJOR: unbound variable", which is how run 33972074753 failed
# on main (issue #115).

: "${NVM_INSTALL_VERSION:?must be passed in by scripts/measure-disk-space.sh}"

log_debug() { [ "$BOX_VERBOSE" = "1" ] && echo -e "\033[0;36m[debug]\033[0m $1" || true; }
log_success() { echo -e "\033[0;32m[✓]\033[0m $1"; }
log_warning() { echo -e "\033[1;33m[!]\033[0m $1"; }

command_exists() { command -v "$1" &>/dev/null; }

install_php() {

fi

cp "$JSON_TMP_COPY" "$JSON_OUTPUT_FILE_ABS"
rm -f "$JSON_TMP_COPY"

# ============================================================================

# Args: component_name category install_command...
measure_install() {
  local name="$1"
  local category="$2"
  shift 2

  log_info "Measuring installation: $name"

  # Cleanup before measurement
  cleanup_for_measurement

  # Record starting disk usage
  local start_bytes
  start_bytes=$(get_disk_usage_bytes)

  # Run installation command
  if "$@"; then
    # Cleanup after installation
    cleanup_for_measurement

    # Record ending disk usage
    local end_bytes
    end_bytes=$(get_disk_usage_bytes)

    # Calculate difference
    local diff_bytes=$((end_bytes - start_bytes))

    # Handle negative values (can happen due to cleanup removing more than installed)
    if [ "$diff_bytes" -lt 0 ]; then
      diff_bytes=0
    fi

    # Convert to MB with decimal precision (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes).
    # Integer floor division via / 1024 / 1024 truncates any component under
    # 1 MiB to 0 MB, which is misleading (e.g. 741 KB shows as 0 MB).
    # Use awk for floating-point division to get precise values (e.g. 0.74 MB).
    # See docs/case-studies/issue-55 for full root cause analysis.
    local diff_mb
    diff_mb=$(awk "BEGIN {printf \"%.2f\", $diff_bytes / 1000000}")

    add_measurement "$name" "$category" "$diff_bytes" "$diff_mb"
    return 0
  else
    log_warning "Installation of $name failed"
    add_measurement "$name" "$category" 0 0
    return 1
  fi
}

# Measure apt package installation
measure_apt_install() {
  local name="$1"
  local category="$2"
  shift 2
  local packages="$*"

# Initialize opam and install Rocq
if command -v opam &>/dev/null; then
  if [ ! -d "$HOME/.opam" ]; then
    log_info "Initializing Opam..."
    opam init --disable-sandboxing --auto-setup -y || true
    log_success "Opam initialized"
  fi

  eval "$(opam env --switch=default 2>/dev/null)" || true

  ROCQ_ACCESSIBLE=false
  if command -v rocq &>/dev/null && rocq -v &>/dev/null; then
    ROCQ_ACCESSIBLE=true
  elif command -v rocqc &>/dev/null; then
    ROCQ_ACCESSIBLE=true
  elif command -v coqc &>/dev/null; then
    ROCQ_ACCESSIBLE=true
  fi

  if [ "$ROCQ_ACCESSIBLE" = false ]; then
    log_info "Installing Rocq Prover (this may take several minutes)..."
    opam repo add rocq-released https://rocq-prover.org/opam/released 2>/dev/null || true
    opam update 2>/dev/null || true

    if opam pin add rocq-prover --yes 2>/dev/null; then
      log_success "Rocq Prover pinned and installed"
    elif opam install rocq-prover -y 2>/dev/null; then
      log_success "Rocq Prover installed via opam install"
    else
      opam install coq -y || true
    fi

    eval "$(opam env --switch=default 2>/dev/null)" || true
  else
